items.title: ¿Qué encuestas aciertan más? Compara los errores y los sesgos de cada encuestadora
items.description: Los sondeos son el mejor instrumento para predecir unas elecciones. Y en España funcionan bien: las encuestas finales se desvían del resultado unos dos puntos por partido. Aunque se las juzga con dureza, lo cierto es que anticipan el voto de un país cuando millones de personas todavía están indecisas. Pero ¿hay encuestadoras más afinadas? ¿Se equivocan siempre al mismo lado? Hoy respondemos esas preguntas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Patty Bonet, estrella de la ONCE: “Solo me ofrecen papeles que dan yuyu, pero soy actriz y tengo que comer”
items.description: Cuando Patty Bonet (Valencia, 41 años) nació, el médico que la trajo al mundo le dijo a sus padres que era una niña muy rubia, muy blanca y ciega. Nada de eso era verdad. Dos años después, un oftalmólogo dio con el diagnóstico correcto: “Su hija es albina , va a tener limitación visual, pero va a poder hacer lo que le dé la gana”. No se equivocaba. Bonet es periodista, presentadora, actriz, conferenciante y activista en favor de la inclusión y la diversidad. Desde hace cuatro años, se cuela cada noche en millones de hogares españoles en pleno prime time para copresentar los sorteos del cupón de la ONCE en Televisión Española. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Llegó la hora de los avatares en las aulas: Harvard clona a sus docentes
items.description: David Shrier no siempre ha sido dueño de su imagen. Cuando este profesor universitario abandonó la antigua institución académica donde impartía clases, esta siguió usando su rostro para promocionar un curso de emprendimiento en línea, con vídeos que él había grabado y sin pagarle nada a cambio. Tuvo que contratar a un abogado para que los retirasen de internet. Pero la idea no se desvaneció tras el pleito. Hoy Shrier enseña en Imperial Business School , en Londres, y cuenta con una réplica digital que responde a sus alumnos a cualquier hora. La conocen como Davatar. “Lo que sé es que ahora mi nombre, mi imagen y mi apariencia me pertenecen”, afirma. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Abel Ferrara, el director maldito que dejó las drogas a los 61: “Mi rehabilitación se basa en dejar de decir mentiras”
items.description: Es un clásico de Brian de Palma, pero hubo un tiempo en que Atrapado por su pasado (1993), el thriller criminal protagonizado por Al Pacino, pudo ser un éxito de Abel Ferrara (Bronx, Nueva York, 75 años). A principios de los noventa el legendario director llevaba un año ensayando con Al Pacino cuando apareció un guionista nuevo. Semanas después, Tom Pollock, jefe de Universal, le llamó aparte durante una cena en un restaurante de Cannes para hablarle de otra nueva versión del guion, lo cual a Ferrara le pareció una tomadura de pelo. Dejó su botella de vino blanco en la mesa de Pollock antes de ir a hablar con él, y al volver la cogió y se la metió dentro de la chaqueta, por esa costumbre neoyorquina de esconder el alcohol al salir a la calle. A los pocos días, le despidieron: alguien fue contando que le había robado una botella a Pollock. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Del ‘vaporwave’ al ‘dreamcore’. Formas de evasión digital que producen una extraña sensación de consuelo
items.description: Piscinas vacías bañadas por una luz amarillenta uniforme. Pasillos infinitos con moqueta verde y luces de neón. Aparcamientos desiertos, centros comerciales abandonados, gimnasios sin gente. Son los espacios liminales , uno de los fenómenos visuales más extraños y persistentes de la cultura de internet en los últimos años: imágenes de lugares cotidianos vaciados de vida humana que generan, a partes iguales, inquietud y una extraña sensación de consuelo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El trampantojo de la ropa agotada: cómo la moda juega con el marketing para generar urgencia de compra
items.description: Siete meses después de darse a conocer la noticia de la colaboración entre Zara y John Galliano, la esperada colección llegó a las tiendas el pasado 1 de octubre. Bajo el título de Re{form} , la primera de las cuatro cápsulas que veremos (concebidas como una reconstrucción de piezas del archivo de Inditex) está formada por 157 artículos entre prendas y accesorios. Más de 80 de las referencias se agotaron en las primeras horas y en ese mismo lapso de tiempo ya se podían encontrar decenas de ellas en portales de venta de ropa como Vinted. Las prendas, impecables y con etiquetas. Los precios, inflados. Uno de los diseños agotados en la web, un abrigo de lana con solapas a contraste y costuras visibles, se vende en segunda mano por 920 euros, casi el triple de sus 399 euros originales. Los guantes largos de tul, a la venta por 29,95 euros y agotados en tienda, se pueden adquirir por casi 100 euros en plataformas de reventa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: De Christy Turlington a Eugenia Silva: por qué el yoga triunfa entre modelos que buscan más que un cuerpo sano
items.description: Cuenta la modelo y empresaria Eugenia Silva (Toledo, 50 años) que hubo una temporada en la que dormía fuera de casa hasta 20 noches al mes. Pero uno de los hábitos que más le mantenía conectada a la tierra, y con la sensación de hogar, durante los 15 años que tuvo su base en Nueva York (de 1999 a 2016) era su práctica semanal de yoga. En una videollamada desde su casa de Madrid, recién llegada de una de sus revisiones tras su operación de cadera (le han incorporado un implante de titanio), recuerda cómo se encontró con esta práctica: “Cuando vivía allí hacía mucho ejercicio: barra de ballet, iba a correr, a escalar al rocódromo... pero sentía que me faltaba algo. No sé cómo me crucé con el Jivamukti Center al que iba Christy Turlington . Estuve practicando durante mucho tiempo allí. Cuando venía a España, en aquella época, siempre buscaba un estudio. A día de hoy, el yoga es mi terapia y mi medicina”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Gold edges higher on softer oil; Fed rate outlook in focus
items.description: Gold prices edged higher on Monday as softer ‌oil prices offered support, while investors assessed the chances of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike later this year and looked for fresh signals on the US central bank’s policy trajectory. Spot gold ​rose 0.3% to $4,175.60 per ounce by 0259 GMT, while US gold futures for December ​delivery gained 0.4% to $4,196.40. “Gold is posting a modest rise to start ⁠the week. The metal is responding positively to the softer tone in oil prices ​from an inflation standpoint,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade. “In the near ​term, a more sustained decline in oil prices or a clearer move lower in yields would be the most constructive catalysts (for gold), as both would ease inflation and rate concerns.” Oil prices slipped on Monday ​after US President Donald Trump waived sanctions and tariffs on Russia that may lead ​to more Russian fuel exports. Meanwhile, US import prices increased more than expected in September, boosted by higher ‌costs for ⁠energy products and a range of other goods, further evidence of rising inflation pressures as the Middle East conflict persists. Market participants now await the Federal Open Market Committee’s meeting on US interest rates and the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data due next week. The ​US central bank tracks ​the PCE price ⁠measures for its 2% inflation target. According to the CME’s FedWatch Tool, traders are pricing in a 16% chance of a rate hike this ​month and a 92% chance of an increase in December. While gold ​is typically ⁠considered a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates reduce the appeal of the non-yielding asset. Elsewhere, the European Central Bank is likely to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at least ⁠one ​more time this year to fight inflationary pressures, the ​International Monetary Fund said on Friday. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.9% to $57.54 per ounce, platinum gained 0.7% to $1,642.29 and ​palladium climbed 1.5% to $1,129.13.

People playing loud music on buses in UK could face £100 fine
items.description: Passengers who play loud music on buses in England could be fined up to £100 under an attempt by the government to crack down on antisocial behaviour. The measures also seek to tackle littering, vaping and threatening behaviour to help improve journeys on all forms of public transport. Offenders on buses could be fined under new powers for local authorities. A national campaign asking rail passengers to “share the carriage, not the noise” is also being launched. The proposed crackdown has been welcomed by campaigners, but some have questioned how it can be enforced. “We’ve all been on the train when someone starts blasting music or videos from their phone. It gets on your nerves and can quickly spoil the journey,” said Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Under existing powers, those who are asked to stop and refuse could be removed from a train or fined up to £1,000. The phenomenon has been given many names, including loudcasting or sodcasting, and in recent years, Ofcom, YouGov and Transport for London (TfL) have all published polls showing that the vast majority of people dislike it. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said small changes in behaviour “can make a massive difference to people’s experience on public transport”. The government said it had issued new guidance to local authorities on powers, introduced earlier this year, to help them crack down on loud music and other antisocial behaviour on buses in England. These new powers allow them to impose new rules on buses, but still need to be signed off by the Transport Secretary Those who commit offences could face fixed penalties of up to £100. The government says bus drivers will not be responsible for enforcing the new rules. It says authorised officers, including Transport Safety Officers and the Police, will deal with the incidents. Meanwhile, a new national campaign aims to remind rail passengers to “share the carriage, not the noise”, to improve journeys for everyone The campaign will be launched across operator websites, social media, and in carriages. The government said this would end the current “patchwork” of approaches across different rail operators, and help create “a clear, consistent message across the network”. The general secretary of the TSSA transport union, Maryam Eslamdoust, said tackling antisocial behaviour on public transport was “a step in the right direction”. However, she added that the government must also “urgently confront the violence, threats and abuse faced by passengers and transport workers”. “Increasing the budget for British Transport Police is vital to protect people, respond to incidents and bring violent offenders to justice,” she said. Michael Solomon Williams from the Campaign for Better Transport told the BBC antisocial behaviour could be a “real deterrent” to people using public transport, especially those with different accessibility needs. He also questioned how the new measures will be enforced. “When local authorities are required to do the enforcement there are perhaps some question marks about how a local police force might be called upon on bus services, for example, where we don’t tend to see British Transport Police.” Richard Holden MP, Shadow Transport Secretary, said: “After we led the charge against antisocial behaviour on public transport last summer, Ministers have worked out that nobody wants to endure pounding techno or blaring hip hop on a packed train or bus. “But passengers and railway staff face far more serious problems. Assaults against rail staff have risen by 68%, while prosecutions have slumped under Labour. It’s time for Andy Burnham to get serious about enforcement, tackling violence and protecting those who work on our railways.” Liberal Democrat Transport spokesperson, Olly Glover MP said: “Tough talk means nothing without enforcement. “Unless the Government funds transport safety officers on the ground, these new rules won’t be worth the paper they’re printed on.” Independent watchdog Transport Focus said research it had published in June showed personal safety and security was now fundamental to passengers’ confidence in the railway. “Four in 10 passengers say that anti-social behaviour has made them feel vulnerable when travelling,” said Alex Campbell, Transport Focus’s director of policy and insight. “Measures that reduce nuisance behaviour, such as playing loud music and vaping, can help improve people’s experience and encourage more people to choose public transport.”

items.title: The commercial cost of Afghan intransigence
items.description: Goods trucks remain parked at the Torkham border’s terminal since its closure amid tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan.—Photo by the writer • From $1.3 billion in FY24-25, bilateral trade has fallen to a little over $350 million in FY25-26 • Traders call for balancing security and commerce needs PESHAWAR: The sprawling terminal at Torkham, built at the cost of several billion rupees, wears a deserted look as a protracted conflict continues to overshadow trade ties between Pakistan and Afghanistan. Islamabad remains adamant that there can be no engagement with Kabul without tangible action against terrorists operating from its soil, but the relationship remains in suspended animation due to the intransigence of the Taliban regime. Industries in Pakistan, especially transport and pharmaceuticals, have been facing heavy losses since the border closed on Oct 12, 2025, following deadly clashes between the two countries. Besides Torkham, other border crossings, including Kharlachi, Ghulam Khan and Angoor Adda in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Chaman in Balochistan, have also remained closed for all kinds of trade. Figures released in July showed that Afghan Transit Trade, which stood at nearly 89,000 containers valued at $5 billion before the return of the Taliban, had plunged to just 11,592 containers worth $367 million in the outgoing fiscal year. According to data on bilateral trade, released by the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP) earlier this year, Pak-Afghan trade witnessed a drop of 74pc in the last fiscal, from one year prior. Figures show that bilateral trade fell from $1.3bn in 2024-25 to $358m in 2025-26. A 95pc decline was recorded in bilateral trade in 2026-27 compared with the previous year, according to the TDAP figures released in August. Pakistani exports to Afghanistan include pharmaceutical products, cement, plastics, rice, fruits and vegetables among others, while major imports include onions, tomatoes, seeds, grapes, dried apricots, apples, coal, and unwrought lead. Junaid Altaf, a former president of the Sarhad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI), said the business community of Khyber Pakht­unkhwa endured increasingly difficult economic challenges due to the prolonged closure of the Pak-Afghan border. “For a province already facing structural economic disadvantages, the closure has not merely disrupted a trade route, it has further weakened the economic opportunities on which its businesses, workers and border communities depend,” he deplored. Mr Altaf said that unlike Karachi and Lahore, Peshawar and the rest of KP faced higher logistics costs for many manufacturing and trading activities. “Being far from seaports and major international shipping gateways adds to the cost of importing raw materials, transporting them to factories, manufacturing finished products and subsequently distributing those products across Pakistan or exporting them to international markets.” Against this backdrop, the Pakistan-Afghanistan trade corridor has historically represented a major economic opportunity for KP, he said, highlighting the potential of KP to become a stronger pharmaceutical production and export centre. The pharmaceutical sector accounted for approximately $130m in exports to Afghanistan in FY23-24, according to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. This figure illustrates that the loss of access to the Afghan market is a significant commercial setback with implications for production, investment and employment. Saying that the KP business community deserved a clear and sustainable way forward, Mr Altaf suggested that the objective should not be trade at any cost, nor should it be indefinite economic isolation. “It should be secure borders, regulated trade, competitive industry and shared prosperity,” he opined. Malik Sohni, president of the All Pakistan Agricultural Produce Traders Federation, said that Afghanistan was a huge market for Pakistani potatoes. Up to 50 trucks carrying potatoes used to cross into Afghanistan daily, while 25 trucks of green vegetables also passed daily, he said, adding that the border closure badly hit the potato market, reducing crop cultivation by almost half. “Potato prices will go up in the coming months as demand will rise against limited supply,” Mr Sohni feared. He claimed that he faced a loss of Rs180m when potato prices crashed after the sudden flare in hostilities. He added that the border closure also affected Pakistani exports to Central Asia. Besides exports and imports, a large number of people from across KP, particularly in Khyber, have been associated with the transport business and they have fallen on hard times as well. Azeemullah, a transporter, said that due to the prolonged border closure, he had to sell three of his five trucks. “The transport sector of KP is nearly ruined,” he lamented, adding that div­erting these trucks to other parts of the country was not economically viable. However, Fuad Ishaq, a Peshawar-based businessman and former president of the SCCI, held different views. “I am of the view that we cannot compromise our security for just $800m in trade a year.” He said Afghanistan had a 45m population, roughly the same as KP, and the items normally exported there could be directed somewhere else. He claimed that cutting off ties with Afghanistan also reduced the burden on hospitals and schools in Pakistan, which he described as a positive development. “We should have trade, but security comes first,” Mr Ishaq stressed. Published in Dawn, October 19th, 2026

items.title: Recriminations grow over failure of PTI protest plan
items.description: • Salman Akram Raja tries to quell talk of ‘disagreement’ among core committee members • Insiders say march date was announced without consultation; protest plans kept under wraps, even from party leaders ISLAMABAD: Controversy over its failure to hold a protest march continues to plague the PTI, with the fallout suggesting differences within its leadership over who is to blame for the botched mobilisation , even as party leaders continued to publicly deny any disarray. With questions mounting, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja turned to social media on Sunday to play down talk of a “disagreement” during a meeting of the party’s core committee and to answer the allegations made against Sohail Afridi, the non-functional chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. “There should be no ambiguity,” Mr Raja wrote on X, calling Mr Afridi “a brave young man” who has stayed steadfast with the ideology of PTI founder Imran Khan. He said, however, that the administrative aspects of the protest march needed to be critically reviewed to counter the “narratives” being propagated against Mr Afridi. He accused critics of presenting core committee discussions “out of context” and distorting them as part of “conspiratorial narratives”. Meanwhile, a senior party leader who attended the meeting and spoke to Dawn on condition of anonymity, painted a less rosy picture. The leader said the party’s core committee meetings had started to discuss why the protest march failed and that the discussion was still ongoing. “On Saturday night, the meeting started after 10pm and ended after 2am. As many as 16 members of the committee got an opportunity to speak, and the remaining will speak in upcoming sessions,” he said. “At the outset, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar said the meeting was called to discuss the current situation and the way forward. However, Raja suggested that they first discuss how the date for the protest march, Sept 27, was announced,” the leader added. “During the meeting, it was revealed that in August, Afridi had called a meeting in KP which was attended by Gohar, Raja, Asad Qaiser, Shafiullah Jan, Mina Khan, Shahid Khatak and Taimur Jhagra,” he said. Afridi had announced that the march would be held on Sept 27 , but this information was leaked to some vloggers subsequently. When criticism started that it had not been discussed in the political committee and core committee, the meetings of both committees were called on the same day, and in the evening Afridi made the announcement at a public meeting. The insider further disclosed that the leadership was kept in the dark regarding the operational strategy for the protest and the party’s broader negotiation tactics. “It was also revealed that Afridi was asked a number of times what the plan was, but he kept his cards close to his chest,” he said. “The meeting also heard that the PTI team had decided to walk out over the issue of terrorism, and when they realised it could trigger criticism, it was decided to use the name of Imran Khan and a meeting with him.” The leader said that during the meeting, Raja asked Ali Asghar Khan, son of the late Air Marshal Asghar Khan, why the party did not hold the protest march after Afridi’s arrest. Ali Asghar Khan, who is PTI secretary general in KP and head of the coordination committee for the protest march, said he was not aware of any such plans. “Asghar claimed that he had asked Afridi and Junaid Akbar many times, but they said details would be shared soon,” the leader said. “It annoyed many members of the core committee, as they said more than 1,400 workers and leaders were arrested under the Maintenance of Public Order law, but PTI in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa did not have any plan.” Another leader said Haleem Adil Sheikh confessed that the opposition was 70 per cent responsible and the government 30pc responsible for the failure of talks. “The agreement was finalised as Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi brought an amended agreement that both sides agreed to without meeting Imran Khan,” he said. “Soon after that, a call also came from Afridi to say that the meeting could not be held without first consulting Imran Khan.” The committee also discussed reports claiming that Barrister Gohar had given approval to establish offices of TTAP at the district level, the leader claimed. “Raoof Hasan objected and asked how it was possible, and Barrister Gohar said that he did not give any such approval.” The source further claimed that during the meeting, Seemabia Tahir suggested that the party should go for another protest march, but a majority of the members said that it was not possible during the current circumstances. When contacted for a response, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram declined to comment on the matter. Published in Dawn, October 19th, 2026

items.title: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going
items.description: US President Donald Trump has said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table. “I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine,” Trump said on his Truth Social messaging platform, adding that he didn’t want to “do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table”. Trump blocked numerous sanctions on Russia on Friday night, two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky deepened. Zelensky told NBC News on Sunday that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a “historic mistake”. Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev has responded to Trump’s order by calling it “an important and truly historic moment”. He said the sanctions, which were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September, would have inflicted “serious damage” on the US and global market. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has described the suspension of the sanctions as a 60-day pause during which their potential impact on the US and global economies would be analysed. In his Truth Social post, Trump also said Zelensky “doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did”, adding “he could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now”. Zelensky has pushed for an end to fighting, and has repeatedly said that Putin doesn’t want peace, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week. Despite the international sanctions, Russia has still been able to export oil, much of it to China and India – often at attractive discounts. According to the think-tank Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), China has taken about half of Russia’s crude exports, with India accounting for about 37%. In remarks to a European Union summit, after Trump announced the deal to buy diesel from Russia and said Zelensky was “more difficult to deal with” than Putin, Zelensky said it was nice to be among “real leaders”. Ukraine’s President Zelensky attended an EU leaders’ summit in Brussels on Friday Zelensky has repeatedly pushed for stringent sanctions to limit funding that Russia can use in its war effort. After the latest move from the US, however, he said he believed the Trump administration would lift more sanctions against Russia. Ukraine and its European allies criticised Trump’s plans to import Russian diesel to help lower US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war. The deal, according to Zelensky, was tantamount to the US investing in Russia’s war effort. Concerns that Trump is siding with Russia have been heightened by disruption to Starlink, a US-provided satellite system used by Ukraine. That hampered Kyiv’s ability to protect itself from Russian attacks. Zelensky said US officials had linked speed restrictions to technical issues. However, he said Ukraine had tested Starlink on EU territory and found it was operating at higher speeds. Trump has denied both deliberately slowing down the network and a further accusation from Zelensky that the US had stopped sharing defence intelligence.

items.title: Pakistan Army officer martyred, 4 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
items.description: Four terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Balochistan’s Kalat district, while a security personnel member was martyred in a targeted attack as security forces conducted a series of operations in Gwadar, the military’s media wing said on Monday. The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement that security forces are conducting a series of operations in areas of Shadi Kaur and Pasni in Gwadar, and Jattakabad in Kalat district, on the reported presence of multiple hideouts of Fitna al Hindustan. The state has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. In the first operation on October 18, security forces conducted an IBO in the general area of Jattakabad, during which four terrorists were eliminated. “A large cache of arms and ammunition was also recovered,” it added. In the second incident, ISPR added that security forces conducted a series of clearance operations in the general area of Shadi Kaur, Pasni, in Gwadar. It added that during one of the operations, the lead force component, led by 34-year-old Major Wajahat Waheed, a resident of Lahore, was martyred in an improvised explosive device attack. “Sanitisation operations will continue to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area. The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-e-Istehkam” , as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue at full pace. “Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” ISPR added. Intensified operations Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, prompting security forces to intensify counterterrorism operations. A day earlier, security forces killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during IBO conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan. On the night of Oct 12/13, security forces busted a terrorist hideout and killed five terrorists during an IBO in Washuk, ISPR said . Days later, Balochistan government officials said that six terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), two would-be female suicide bombers, and two commanders of a banned organisation had been arrested during IBOs across the province. They said around 90 arrested terrorists were being held at a centre where investigations and legal proceedings were under way. Earlier this month, five terrorists were eliminated in Balochistan’s Mastung district, state media reported . The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August , according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS). As per the report, Balochistan was declared the province “most affected” by terrorism.

items.title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff survives shooting in Mumbai
items.description: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff has survived a shooting in Mumbai and has not sustained any gunshot wounds, according to Indian police who are investigating the incident. The 36-year-old was shot at on Sunday evening, while he was in a car that was leaving a football club in the suburb of Juhu. Several news outlets have published a video showing at least two gunmen firing multiple shots at close range at the front passenger seat of a car while it is slowly moving past a crowd. The incident has heightened concern about the safety of public figures in India, with some killed or injured in targeted attacks in recent years. “These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated, and we will put an end to this hooliganism,” said Eknath Shinde, deputy chief minister of Maharashtra state, where Mumbai is located. He paid a visit to Shroff after the shooting on Sunday evening, and said the actor and his mother had been left “shaken” by the attack. Police said two people were injured in the shooting, including Shroff’s driver, local media reported. This is the latest in a string of attacks on some of the country’s biggest public figures in recent years. In 2024, police in India arrested two members of a criminal gang for a gun attack targeting the home of Bollywood actor Salman Khan. That same year, influential Indian politician Baba Siddique was shot dead in Mumbai. The son of two actors, Tiger Shroff made his acting debut in 2014 with the romance film Heropanti and went on to star in several films. He is also a football enthusiast who plays for the professional football club Mumbay FC.

items.title: Threat forces Israel to Austria flight into emergency landing
items.description: An Austrian Airlines flight from Israel to Austria has been forced to divert to Bulgaria after a reported bomb threat. The Airbus A320 plane was travelling from Tel Aviv to Vienna on Sunday night but made an emergency landing in Sofia, where passengers were evacuated, the Bulgarian transport ministry said in a statement. The Bulgarian air force scrambled a MiG-29 fighter jet to escort the airliner, the transport ministry said. No injuries have been reported and an investigation has begun. It comes after a pilot attempted to hijack a Flydubai flight en route to Tel Aviv last month by attacking the captain, before the flight’s crew and passengers overpowered him and landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia. Bulgarian and Israeli media reported that a bomb threat had been made. Austrian Airlines has confirmed a threat was made, without giving further details. A spokesperson told the AFP news agency there were 51 passengers and six crew members on board the jet. Authorities conducted a security search of the plane after it landed in Sofia, about 30 minutes from when the alert was first raised. It was over Romania when it diverted to Sofia. Flight tracking data showed Austrian Airlines 82 left Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv on Sunday evening before landing at Vasil Levski airport in Sofia three hours later. Last week, Croatia and Germany both scrambled fighter jets after a commercial flight from the Greek holiday island of Corfu to the German city of Nuremberg accidentally sent out a hijacking alert. The BBC has sought further comment from Lufthansa, the owner of Austrian Airlines.

items.title: Microsoft pulls out of UK’s largest AI data centre
items.description: A tech company has said it still plans to build the UK’s largest AI data centre despite Microsoft’s withdrawal from the project. Nscale announced last year it had pledged £2bn to build and open a pioneering facility in Loughton , Essex. However, the BBC understands that Microsoft, which said it would fund a supercomputer at the site, has terminated its involvement. A spokesperson for Nscale said it was exploring alternative power sources and its relationship with Microsoft remained strong for their other projects together overseas. Microsoft declined to comment. “We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK,” Nscale said. “Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term.” The data centre was due to receive its power supply at the end of the year. But as first reported by the Telegraph on Sunday , Nscale has been told this will not happen until the 2030s. “This unfortunate London-wide grid issue has no impact on our other contracts,” Nscale told the BBC. Nscale and Microsoft are still working together on projects in Norway, Portugal and the United States. The Loughton site is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it eventually opens. Only last month, Microsoft announced that some of the $30bn (£22bn) it was investing in the UK would be used to fund the Loughton supercomputer.

items.title: Pakistan stresses diplomacy as Iran rejects US ‘threats’
items.description: • Dar discusses evolving regional situation in call with Araghchi • Iranian FM says Tehran rejects intimidation but remains open to dialogue • Insists seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal remains on table • Pakistani, Egyptian FMs condemn Houthi attacks, discuss R-4 coordination • Iran’s new defence minister threatens ‘enormous damage’ to US if attacks renewed ISLAMABAD: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Sunday stressed the need for continued dialogue and diplomacy in a telephone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as regional tensions persisted amid the US-Iran conflict and renewed fighting in Yemen. The Foreign Office said the two ministers discussed the evolving regional situation as well as the ongoing meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad. Mr Dar “underscored the importance of continued dialogue and diplomacy in addressing regional challenges”, the FO said, adding that the two sides agreed to remain in close contact. Mr Dar also held a telephone conversation with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and exchanged views on recent regional developments. The ministers strongly condemned Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed their solidarity with the kingdom as well as support for its sovereignty, territorial integrity and security. They also discussed cooperation under the Regional Four (R-4) framework comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. The two ministers looked forward to the next R-4 meeting to coordinate further on regional issues. Iran rejects ‘threats’ Meanwhile, Mr Arag­hchi told the OIC meeting in Baghdad that Iran “does not accept coercion, threats, or intimidation” by the US and “will not relinquish its sovereign rights under pressure”. “But it remains ready for dialogue based on mutual respect and credible guarantees,” he added. Speaking to the media in Baghdad, Mr Araghchi said Iran’s offer to reopen the strategic waterway within seven days remained on the table. “Our situation is clear and based on the seven-day proposal presented to the US. They shared comments which we are reviewing, but our proposal is still on the table,” Mr Araghchi said. He said that if the US showed “honesty”, the path towards reopening the Strait of Hormuz was clear. Iran’s conditions incl­ude lifting the US blockade on its ports, removing sanctions on its oil exports and ending hostilities across regional fronts. Mr Araghchi added that if Washington accepted Tehran’s conditions, the strait could reopen within six days, followed by the resumption of talks the next day. US warned Iran’s newly appointed defence minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi warned that any renewed US military attack would cause “enormous damage” to Washington and its regional allies. “People can rest assured that they will most likely not dare to attack us,” Mr Akhlaghi told reporters shortly after securing parliament’s vote of confidence. “If they do, they themselves and the region will suffer enormous damage,” he said. Published in Dawn, October 19th, 2026

items.title: Families wait for answers after Nigerian military plane crash
items.description: More than a week after a Nigerian Air Force plane crash killed all 25 people on board, families say they are still ​waiting for answers as military teams search for wreckage and human remains in swampy terrain. President Bola Tinubu has ordered an ‌investigation into the October 5 crash , but relatives say they have received little information about what caused it, whether remains have been identified or how recovery efforts are progressing. The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) said the aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos when it crashed in a remote area of southwest ​Nigeria after losing radar contact. It has not disclosed the cause. The flight was carrying 19 military personnel and six civilians. For ​London-based software developer Victor Anii, the uncertainty has compounded the grief of losing his older sister, Esther ⁠Anii, a sergeant in the Nigerian Air Force. When he woke on October 5, he found a message from Esther asking him to send ​money for a bus journey from Benin City to Lagos. She told him the group had flown from Abuja but stopped in Benin City ​because of a fault with the aircraft. Tired of waiting, she was considering continuing the journey by road. Hours later, news broke that an NAF aircraft flying between the two cities had crashed . “We didn’t know what was going on. We just knew we couldn’t reach her, and her husband couldn’t reach some of his friends ​on the flight,” he said. It was not until the following day, when the Air Force published a list of those on board, that ​the family learned Esther had been among those killed. WAITING FOR ANSWERS Frustrated by what he saw as poor communication from the authorities, Anii posted a video ‌online criticising ⁠the Air Force’s handling of families after the crash. Two days later, he said, an NAF commander visited his parents’ home in Abuja carrying two envelopes. One contained a condolence letter. The family did not open the second because they suspected it contained cash. “Whatever that is in it is not enough to take away the pain of my family,” he said. Asked about support for relatives and efforts to identify remains, NAF spokesperson Ehimen Ejodame referred Reuters to Air Force statements saying it had pledged support to families and intensified search and recovery operations. He did not address the allegation that money was offered. Damilola Folorunsho, whose 36-year-old brother, Sunday, was among the six civilians on board, said no one had contacted her family. “My mum has been living with me since the incident,” she said. The ​family, who live about ⁠200 km (125 miles) from the Igbokoda swamp crash site, do not know whether his remains have been recovered or how far the investigation has progressed. NAF did not respond to questions about whether it is standard practice for military aircraft to carry civilians. The crash is the latest in a series ⁠of Nigerian ​military aviation accidents that have raised questions about safety and accountability. A review ​of publicly reported incidents shows at least nine NAF aircraft accidents had killed more than 30 people in the five years before the latest crash. For Anii, accountability matters more than ​compensation. “The most important thing now is to know what happened and ensure it never happens again.”

items.title: Tunisians stage biggest protest in years against President Saied
items.description: Thousands of Tunisians joined the largest protest against President Kais Saied in years in the capital on Saturday, accusing ​him of undermining democracy and mishandling the economy in a growing challenge to his ‌rule. The demonstration, led by the major UGTT labour union and civil society groups, comes as Tunisia grapples with an economic crisis, worsening public services, recurring water and power cuts, and shortages of medicines and essential goods. Saied ​seized broad powers in 2021 and 2022, dissolving parliament, dismissing dozens of judges and ​ruling by decree, moves that opponents described as a coup. Rights groups say he has ⁠intensified a crackdown on civil society, journalists and opposition figures. Saied rejects those allegations, ​saying he is not a dictator, and has accused his opponents of engineering economic crises ​to fuel social unrest. In a rare show of unity, opposition parties from across the political spectrum joined lawyers, doctors , journalists, unemployed people and civil society groups in marching along Habib Bourguiba Avenue, a focal point ​of the 2011 protests that helped trigger the Arab Spring uprisings. The protest poses a significant challenge to Saied after years of division have weakened the opposition’s ability to mobilise large crowds. “Silence will ‌no longer ⁠be acceptable … the state cannot be built by concentrating all powers in the hands of one person”, Slah Eddine Salmi, head of the UGTT, told the rally. Hundreds of police were deployed across the capital. Protesters chanted: “No fear, power belongs to the people!” and “The prisons are full, ​people are hungry!”. They ​also revived the ⁠iconic slogan of the 2011 uprising, which in Tunisia was notably peaceful: “The people want the fall of the regime!” They called for the release of Saied’s critics and demanded an end to what they described as attacks on trade union rights. Some carried banners expressing frustration over unemployment and pollution. “Enough is enough! The country is collapsing. We suffer from power and water cuts, and one crisis after another,” said Yassine Gharseli, a ⁠protester ​from Sfax, about 250 km (155 miles) south of Tunis. “I ​came from Sfax to stand up for my freedom and I’m not about to give up, even if I become the ​last voice in the country.”

items.title: Pêche côtière et artisanale : hausse de 23% des débarquements au port de Larache
items.description: Les débarquements de la pêche côtière et artisanale au niveau du port de Larache ont atteint 13.856 tonnes (T) à fin septembre 2026, en hausse de 23% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente, selon l'Office national des pêches (ONP). La valeur marchande de ces captures a reculé de 1% à plus de 254,18 millions de dirhams (MDH), contre environ 256,07 MDH à fin septembre 2025, a précisé l'ONP dans son dernier rapport sur les statistiques sur la pêche côtière et artisanale au Maroc. Par espèce, les quantités de poissons pélagiques débarquées dans ce port ont augmenté de 26% à fin septembre dernier à 11.232 T, pour une valeur estimée à 73 MDH, contre plus de 70,14 MDH/ 8.944 T soit +4% en glissement annuel. Les débarquements des poissons blancs ont, quant à eux, progressé de 30% à 722 T, pour une valeur de plus de 35,71 MDH, contre plus de 33,51 MDH, +7% en glissement annuel. Concernant les débarquement des céphalopodes, ils ont stagné à 972 T pour des recettes de 95,02 MDH (-9%), tandis que pour les crustacés, les débarquements ont augmenté de 11% à 930 T, générant des revenus d'environ 50,45 MDH (+5%). Au niveau national, les débarquements des produits commercialisés de la pêche côtière et artisanale se sont établis à 965.832 T à fin septembre dernier, en hausse de 19% par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente. En valeur, ces débarquements ont augmenté de 6% à plus de 8,68 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) contre environ 8,20 MMDH en glissement annuel. En valeur, ces débarquements ont augmenté de 1% à plus de 7,43 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) contre environ 7,37 MMDH en glissement annuel. items.title: Morocco’s new government has new finance minister, keeps foreign, interior ministers unchanged
items.description: Morocco’s football federation chief and former budget minister Fouzi Lekjaa was appointed economy and finance minister in the country’s new government, formed following the September 23 parliamentary elections , state news agency MAP reported. Lekjaa, a member of the liberal-centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), joins a 32-member government led by Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, whom King Mohammed VI appointed last month as the country’s first woman head of government after PAM won the largest share of seats in parliament. PAM formed a coalition with ​the moderate socialist parties PPS and USFP, and the nationalist Istiqlal. Together ​, they hold 207 seats in parliament, above the 198 needed for a majority. The new government retained the foreign affairs and interior ministers in their posts, MAP ​reported following the government appointment ceremony chaired by King Mohammed ​VI. The lineup also retained the ministers responsible for justice, water, defence, industry and ‌transport. Among ⁠the newcomers, PPS leader Nabil Benabdallah returned to government as education minister, while fellow PPS member Charafat Afailal was named energy minister. Other newcomers included Khalid Hatimi as minister of agriculture, maritime fisheries and ​food sovereignty. The new government will oversee the final stages of a $20-billion push to prepare for the 2030 World Cup , which Morocco will co-host with Portugal and Spain. It faces pressure to address unemployment and demands for better education and health services, which fuelled the Gen Z youth protests last year and the Ceuta migration crisis in July. The new government , however, ⁠is not ​expected to change policy direction in ​Morocco, a constitutional monarchy where the king retains sweeping powers over foreign policy and defence.

items.title: Economy: Roadside restaurants drop food quantity, forcing customers to cut budgets
items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The aroma of smoky jollof rice and boiling pepper soup still wafts through the bustling lanes of various busy business locations in Nigeria, but the portions being served tell a grim story of survival. Read Also: Economy&Lifestyle discovered that as skyrocketing inflation continues to erode the purchasing power of average Nigerians, roadside food vendors across major cities are forcing a tough compromise on their customers. They dish out smaller portions of food at very high costs, amid complaints by artisans, who form the bulk of their customers. For decades, Nigeria’s vibrant informal food sector, locally known as ‘buka’ or ‘mama put’, has been the saving grace of low and middle-income workers looking for affordable, hearty meals. Today, that safety net is fraying. Driven by the removal of fuel subsidies, currency depreciation and soaring transportation costs, food inflation, despite being slow in rate, has forced vendors to restructure their business models just to stay afloat. But the artisans are complaining Emmanuel Osarumwense, a structural technician, looks disappointed as his plate arrives. He explained the cause of his disappointment to Economy&Lifestyle, saying: “Before, N1,000 food from Mama Rukayat would fill my stomach completely, gesturing toward his plate. “Now, I spend N1,500 and I leave the table still feeling hungry. “I have to drink two sachets of water right after eating just to feel heavy. It is survival eating. “We are no longer eating to enjoy; we are eating so we don’t collapse.” Mr. Sunday Agbonkhese, a bricklayer, said: “Before, you can get cooked beans (ewa agoyin) and bread with N700. “You will be full. But now, that N700 can hardly get you a loaf of bread to make you full. “To get full now, you will need up to N3,000 for a meal of bread and beans. “After eating this, which is also a small portion, compared to a few years back, I don’t eat for the rest of the day till evening. “I eat twice a day now just to be able to save a little from my earning which is also little. “It is only God that is feeding me.” Why the portions are shrinking Mrs. Kudirat Adeyemi, who has operated a popular food canteen for over 12 years, stares at her large aluminum pots. According to her, a year ago, a single standard scoop of rice alongside a piece of beef cost N800. But today, maintaining that same quantity would require her to charge N2,000; a price her regular customers, mostly motorcycle riders and traders, simply cannot afford. “If I increase the price to what it actually costs to cook this food, nobody will buy. “So, I had to change the strategy. “The price is now N1,200, but the portion is nearly half of what it used to be. “The piece of meat is smaller, and the rice spoon is no longer heaped. “My customers complain bitterly, but they know it is not my fault. “Even sales have reduced because now I cook two rubbers, almost 5 kg of rice compared to 25kg I was cooking before. “The market is hot.” The reality is visible on the plates of her patrons. What used to be a mountain of rice that could sustain a manual laborer for an entire day has shrunk to a modest mound. Customers adapt to survive The reduction in food portions has drastically altered the eating habits of consumers, many of whom have seen their disposable incomes evaporate. With salaries stagnant and the cost of basic commodities tripling, eating has transformed from a convenient necessity into an exercise in strict budgeting. Economists point out that the food vendor crisis is a direct reflection of a deeper macro-economic strain. The cost of a bag of rice, a staple food in Nigerian households, has hit record high ranging from N60,000 to N100,000, while prices of cooking gas, tomatoes, onions, and vegetable oil have followed a similar trajectory. Many food vendors have closed their shops entirely because they lack the capital to restock. For those remaining, portion control is the only alternative to bankruptcy. A food truck owner, Musa Ibrahim opined that reducing quantities is an act of desperation rather than profit-seeking. “Every morning at the market, the prices of ingredients change. A basket of pepper that was N25,000 last week can increase to N35,000 next week. “If the quantity of food on the plate is not reduced, food vendors will be cooking at a loss and we won’t have money to buy ingredients tomorrow. “Our customers’ pockets are dwindling, so we must give them what their money can buy, even if it is just a few spoons.” Until structural changes occur in agriculture, security, f, both vendors and consumers are trapped in a cycle of diminishing returns. For now, the plates at Nigeria’s food stalls will likely remain light, serving as a stark, daily reminder of the economic pressures squeezing the nation’s tables. items.title: France burns: 143-yr-old City Hall destroyed as cost-of-living protests turn violent
items.description: By Nkiruka Nnorom with agency reports France is reeling under the most violent protests in decades after the historic town hall of Limoges, a 19th-century landmark that survived two World Wars, was largely destroyed Saturday night, after masked protesters set it ablaze during nationwide demonstrations against the high cost of living. Footage showed the moment the bell tower and roof collapsed as flames engulfed the 143-year-old building, inaugurated in 1883 and modelled after Paris City Hall. What began last month as a peaceful student protest spiralled into a national crisis that caught the French government by surprise. High school students had clashed with police over long hours, missing teachers, dilapidated classrooms and an opaque university admissions system. Pupils routinely miss months of teaching due to unfilled staff absences. For four weeks, they marched and barricaded schools. On Saturday, the movement broadened with parents, teachers, grandparents, workers and members of the General Confederation of Labour (CGT) joining them. They carried banners saying the government was not listening and called for more money for public services, lower prices, higher pensions and boosted wages. Other demonstrators joined to voice anger over fuel prices after the Israeli-US war on Iran caused the effective closure of the strait of Hormuz. Tens of thousands marched peacefully in Paris, supporting the schoolchildren’s demands. But separately, masked groups staging moving gatherings, burning barricades and clashing with police overwhelmed the state. According to the Haute-Vienne prefecture, about 2,000 demonstrators gathered in Limoges, with a group breaking into the town hall around 6pm, setting a police car on fire outside before smashing windows and starting the blaze inside. AFP quoted the Haute-Vienne prefecture Prefect, Maurice Barate, as saying: “The roof has collapsed onto lower floors, except the west wing, and two-thirds of the exterior has already disappeared.” He described it as a “catastrophe for heritage” and a “deliberate act by hooligans.” Other national symbols torched, destroyed Besides Limoges, other symbols of the French Republic were also torched, depicting the scale of destruction. In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, protesters torched the historic tourist office on Place Bellecour. In Marseille, black-clad rioters stormed the city hall, overturned furniture and toppled a bust of Marianne, the female personification of the French Republic, and surrounded a municipal police station. In Bordeaux, rioters broke into and ransacked the official residence of the prefect of Gironde, setting fire in the courtyard, forcing authorities to deploy the elite RAID unit. In Lille, municipal buildings were targeted and a group forced its way into the town hall, while attempts were also reported in Calais and Brest. Nothing justifies unbridled violence—Macron Reacting to the riot yesterday, French President, Emmanuel Macron, declared that nothing justified the violence seen in nationwide protests over the rising cost of living and other grievances, even as he called on political bodies to condemn violence. Speaking in an address to the nation, Macron reiterated his earlier stance that people who destroyed government buildings would be held accountable and pay for their crime. He noted that there must be a distinction between protesters with legitimate demands and those who destroyed, smashed, and looted. He vowed to hold accountable those who ‘sought to bring down the Republic’ “Tonight, we all feel anger and shame. Those who looted will have to pay back for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable.” He pointed to unrestrained violence”by “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.” In Grenoble, the city hall was also damaged, prompting the Interior Minister, Laurent Nuñez, and Prime Minister Lecornu to say there was “a clear aim to hit public buildings in many cities.” Govt in crisis talks following violent protest Meanwhile, the French government was in crisis talks yesterday after a day of unrest left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and more than 2,000 people arrested. Interior Minister, Laurent Nunez, said several hundred shops had been damaged, more than 600 police, firefighters and paramedics hurt, and over 2,000 people arrested. In Paris alone, police said a record 855 people were arrested. One 17-year-old boy had his right hand blown off by a crowd-control grenade in Saint-Étienne. One protester died after suffering cardiac arrest in Paris. Ministers as well as police faced pressure for being caught unprepared, while politicians on the left and right called for Nunez’s resignation. In Limoges, Mayor Guillaume Guérin said the attackers “were not demonstrators that defend causes but people organised for war, who told a caretaker he would be killed and told officials they would burn.” Guerin said: “Around 3:30pm our municipal police, although present in number, found themselves no longer able to fight against the violence of rioters because they had run out of munition.’’ He called this a colossal failure of the state and threatened to resign if funds for repair were not provided. In Marseille, where masked groups stormed city hall and a police station, Socialist Mayor, Benoît Payan, said: “Hordes of rioters and looters attacked our common buildings… with no real demands, but with the sole aim to wreck the demands of those who had demonstrated legitimately.” He said questions must be asked about policing tactics. In Lyon, where the historic tourist office was torched, Green Mayor, Grégory Doucet, told Le Monde: “I’m stunned by the violence against public and state property. Shop-owners felt abandoned.” President Emmanuel Macron, who is nearing the end of his second term and will leave office in 2027, wrote on social media there was “no place for violence” and will address the nation. He vowed: “Those who carried out vandalism, attacked administrative offices or businesses, or carried out looting, even in our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished.” His government and far-right frontrunner, Marie Le Pen, blamed ultra-left groups and criminals. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said the government would not be intimidated by violence. Radical-left leader, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, accused the government of organisational failings that “opened the door to chaos”. Yesterday, burnt-out cars, smashed shop windows and the remains of barricades littered Paris, Lille, Bordeaux, Nice, Marseille and Strasbourg. Traders’ unions said over 1,500 shops were ransacked, with losses running into tens of millions of euros. items.title: Espace AES : Les douanes accélèrent l’harmonisation de leurs procédures
items.description: La 5ᵉ réunion des directeurs généraux des douanes de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES) et de l’Office togolais des recettes (OTR), couplée à la 3ᵉ réunion du Comité de pilotage des projets d’interconnexion informatique entre l’AES et le Togo, a pris fin le 16 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Les travaux ont notamment permis de finaliser l’avant-projet de décision instituant le régime tarifaire préférentiel confédéral et fixant les règles d’origine au sein de l’AES, tout en définissant de nouvelles mesures destinées à fluidifier les échanges commerciaux et à renforcer l’interconnexion des systèmes douaniers. La cérémonie de clôture a été présidée par la ministre déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatimata Bako/Traoré, qui a réaffirmé l’engagement du Burkina Faso en faveur du renforcement de la coopération douanière dans l’espace confédéral. Parmi les principales avancées figure la finalisation de l’avant-projet de décision instituant le régime tarifaire préférentiel confédéral et fixant les règles d’origine au sein de l’AES. Ce texte encadre notamment les procédures d’agrément et de certification, ainsi que les éléments constitutifs du prix départ usine. Afin de sécuriser les transactions commerciales, les participants ont également retenu le recours à des certificats d’origine sécurisés intégrant des dispositifs de protection tels que le guillochage, les codes QR et les codes-barres. Par ailleurs, la feuille de route de la deuxième année de la Confédération fait du régime tarifaire préférentiel, du transit des marchandises au sein de l’AES et de l’accord d’assistance administrative mutuelle des priorités. Interconnexion informatique : neuf recommandations réalisées En matière d’interconnexion informatique, le Comité de pilotage a relevé des avancées dans la mise en œuvre des 18 recommandations issues de la session de Bamako. Neuf ont été réalisées, six sont en cours d’exécution et trois restent à reprendre. Les travaux ont également porté sur plusieurs leviers destinés à renforcer la continuité opérationnelle et la fluidité des échanges. Il s’agit notamment de la réflexion sur le système unique de suivi des marchandises (tracking) proposé par le Togo, de l’harmonisation des critères du Cadre de partenariat privilégié pour la reconnaissance mutuelle des opérateurs économiques, de la promotion de la conteneurisation et du transit électronique sans rupture de charge, avec l’appui de la Conférence des Nations unies sur le commerce et le développement (CNUCED). En marge des travaux, la Chambre de commerce et d’industrie du Burkina Faso a présenté le Projet de promotion de la conteneurisation en Afrique de l’Ouest (PPCAO), une initiative saluée par les administrations douanières participantes. De nouvelles mesures opérationnelles à l’horizon 2027 Plusieurs décisions ont été prises afin de consolider l’interopérabilité des systèmes douaniers. Les pays membres devront transmettre les listes des entreprises en vue de la mise en production du code d’identifiant régional au plus tard le 1ᵉʳ janvier 2027. Un nouvel itinéraire de transit reliant Lomé à Djado, via Sanvee-Condji et Tounga, a également été créé pour faciliter l’approvisionnement du Niger à partir du Togo. Sur le plan organisationnel, une cellule technique chargée de superviser en continu les flux d’interconnexion devra être opérationnelle au plus tard le 31 janvier 2027. Par ailleurs, une mission de terrain composée de directeurs adjoints et de chefs de projet est prévue à Cinkansé le 15 novembre 2026. Elle aura pour objectif d’évaluer les infrastructures de stationnement et de contribuer à la résorption des principaux goulets d’étranglement logistiques. Une visioconférence avec la CNUCED, consacrée au projet de migration vers SYDONIA ASY5, est également prévue d’ici à mars 2027. En parallèle, des discussions en vue d’une interconnexion avec le Ghana doivent être engagées. Le Burkina Faso réaffirme son engagement À la clôture des travaux, la ministre déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatimata Bako/Traoré, a réaffirmé l’ambition du Burkina Faso de contribuer au renforcement de la coopération douanière et à l’intégration économique dans l’espace AES. « Notre ambition doit être de faire de l’espace confédéral un espace économique mieux organisé, plus sûr et favorable au développement de nos capacités productives », a-t-elle soutenu. Elle a par ailleurs salué les directeurs généraux des douanes de l’AES pour la qualité des travaux et les a invités à veiller à la mise en œuvre effective des décisions prises. « Je vous invite à maintenir cet esprit de collaboration et à donner aux décisions prises les moyens humains, techniques, organisationnels et financiers nécessaires à leur mise en œuvre. Je réitère mes remerciements aux délégations du Mali, du Niger et de la République togolaise, aux experts, aux équipes techniques et aux structures partenaires pour leur participation », a-t-elle déclaré. La prochaine réunion conjointe des responsables douaniers est prévue à Niamey, au Niger, en octobre 2027. items.title: Cotton arrivals jump 7.5pc as textile crisis deepens
items.description: • Industry says 500 ginning factories, over 150 textile mills closed • Ginners allege imported inputs meant for re-export are being sold locally LAHORE: Cotton arrivals at ginning factories rose 7.53 per cent year-on-year to 4.08 million bales by Oct 15, but the domestic cotton and textile industries are facing a deepening crisis, with around 500 ginning factories, over 150 textile mills and nearly half of the country’s power looms reportedly lying idle. Industry representatives have attributed the crisis to rising production costs and alleged misuse of the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS), under which imported yarn and fabric are reportedly being sold in the domestic market instead of being re-exported. According to the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA), arrivals reached 4,081,265 bales by Oct 15, up 285,628 bales from 3,795,637 bales a year earlier. Punjab recorded arrivals of 1.64m bales, up 7.79pc, while Sindh’s arrivals increased 7.35pc to 2.44m bales. Bahawalnagar led Punjab with 418,750 bales, followed by Bahawalpur with 294,606, Dera Ghazi Khan 236,514, Rahim Yar Khan 169,949 and Layyah 122,327. In Sindh, Sanghar topped the list with 1.14m bales, followed by Sukkur with 264,500 bales, Naushehro Feroze 223,200 and Khairpur 213,900. A total of 471 ginning factories were operational nationwide. Textile mills had purchased around 3.45m bales and exporters 97,000 bales, leaving 531,530 bales unsold. Arrivals during the preceding fortnight totalled 872,863 bales. However, Cotton Ginners Forum Chairman Ihsanul Haq warned that adverse weather could leave national production below initial estimates. He also pointed to a discrepancy between PCGA figures and those of the Punjab Crop Reporting Service, which put provincial production at 2.983m bales against the PCGA’s 1.638m bales in arrivals by Oct 15. Mr Haq said the alleged misuse of the EFS, coupled with rising production costs, had undermined the domestic industry. He cited estimates that 40m to 50m metres of fabric had been imported from China alone under the scheme, while exports had shown little corresponding growth. Figures released by the All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (Aptma) showed man-made yarn imports rising from 3,056 tonnes in the first quarter of 2025-26 to 12,773 tonnes in the corresponding quarter of 2026-27. Man-made fabric imports increased from 660 tonnes to 8,628 tonnes over the same period. Mr Haq alleged that some imports intended for re-export were instead being sold locally, where an 18pc sales tax applied, putting domestic manufacturers at a disadvantage. Aptma has welcomed Customs action against alleged misuse of the scheme and called for restrictions on imports of man-made yarn and fabric under the EFS. It said around 500 ginning factories and more than 150 textile mills had closed, while nearly half of the country’s power looms were inactive. Sajid Mahmood, head of the Transfer of Technology Department at the Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan, said cotton revival required policies focused not only on production but also on farmers’ profitability, production costs, market access and lint quality. If cotton continued to offer lower returns than competing crops, farmers could reduce acreage in the next season, he warned. With 15 to 20 days of picking remaining, he urged farmers to follow agricultural experts’ advice to protect yields and quality. The CCRI has recommended a spray containing 2kg of urea per 100 litres of water in fields with eight to 10 green bolls per plant to encourage boll opening. Farmers should also monitor pink bollworm infestation, pick mature bolls promptly and harvest in dry weather to prevent contamination. Mr Mahmood said the success of cotton revival should be measured by farmers’ net income per acre, not merely the volume of arrivals at ginning factories. Karachi Cotton Brokers Forum leader Naseem Usman urged the government not only to announce a cotton support price but also to devise a procurement mechanism in case market prices fell below the support level. He hoped that the undocumented cotton business would see a decline this year due to strict government measures and might lead to some increase in the overall cotton production. Published in Dawn, October 19th, 2026

items.title: 18 marble workers abducted in Khuzdar
items.description: QUETTA: As many as 18 labourers working at a marble mine in the Naal area, about 40 kilometres from Khuzdar city, were kidnapped on Sunday, police said. A large group of armed men entered the mine premises, held the labourers at gunpoint and abducted 18 of them, along with the son of a mine factory’s owner, officials said. The abductors also opened fire on a worker when he attempted to flee, they added. The abducted labourers are locals from the Wadh and Naal areas. The mine belongs to Sardar Alam Khan Bizenjo, son of Sardar Aslam Bizenjo, the tribal chief of the Bizenjo tribe. Aslam Bizenjo is affiliated with the National Party and has served as a minister in several Balochistan governments. While fleeing the scene, the armed men also took away a loader and two vehicles, officials said. Officials said security forces had launched a search operation in the area to trace the abd­u­cted labourers. No group has so far claimed res­ponsibility for the kidnapping. Published in Dawn, October 19th, 2026

items.title: Igor Martynov, ambassadeur de Russie au Burkina : « Le 3e sommet Russie-Afrique constituera une étape importante dans le partenariat d’égal à égal »
items.description: Le 3e Sommet Russie-Afrique se tient, les 28 et 29 octobre prochain, à Moscou. A l’occasion, nous vous proposons une tribune de l’ambassadeur de la Fédération de Russie au Burkina Faso, Igor Martynov. Les 28 et 29 octobre 2026, Moscou accueillera le Troisième sommet Russie-Afrique, qui a pour objectif d’analyser l’état des relations russo-africaines et de leur donner un nouvel élan, compte tenu de l’évolution rapide de la situation sur le continent africain. Les relations russo-africaines ont des racines profondes dans l’histoire. C’est en effet l’Union soviétique qui a joué un rôle de premier plan dans l’adoption de la Déclaration des Nations unies sur l’octroi de l’indépendance aux pays et aux peuples coloniaux, puis qui a systématiquement contribué à l’émergence des jeunes Etats africains, au développement de leurs économies nationales, ainsi qu’à la mise en place de systèmes d’éducation et de santé. Il est symbolique que la Fédération de Russie, en tant que successeur de l’URSS, plaide activement, à l’ONU et dans d’autres instances internationales, en faveur d’un renforcement du rôle des pays africains. Nous considérons comme inaliénable le droit des Africains à déterminer eux-mêmes leurs voies et leurs modèles de développement, ainsi qu’à choisir leurs partenaires internationaux. Nous soutenons la consolidation des efforts des Etats africains et la création d’unions et d’associations panafricaines visant à faire du continent africain un pôle d’influence au sein d’un ordre mondial multipolaire. La Russie et l’Afrique sont des alliés historiques dans les relations internationales. Nous appelons les colonisateurs occidentaux à rendre des comptes pour le pillage des pays et l’extermination des populations africaines. Nous saluons une implication plus large des pays africains dans les activités du groupe BRICS, qui joue un rôle de plus en plus important dans la promotion des aspirations collectives du Sud Global et de la majorité mondiale. Dans l’esprit du principe « des solutions africaines aux problèmes africains », nous contribuons au règlement des conflits régionaux et au renforcement des capacités des Etats du continent à lutter contre le terrorisme, ainsi que contre d’autres menaces et défis. Nous n’avons pratiquement aucun différend avec aucun pays africain. Je tiens à souligner que le niveau de confiance mutuelle entre nos peuples est très élevé. Tout d’abord parce que nous n’avons jamais exploité l’Afrique, ni considéré ce continent comme une simple source de matières premières. Au contraire, nous accordons la priorité à la mise en œuvre de projets d’investissement qui aident les pays africains à exploiter leurs propres ressources, à renforcer leurs capacités industrielles et à améliorer la qualité de vie de leur population. Nous accordons une grande importance à la coopération commerciale, économique et en matière d’investissements. Il est réjouissant de constater que les échanges commerciaux avec l’Afrique connaissent une croissance soutenue. A l’heure actuelle, nos priorités sont les suivantes: accroître les échanges de marchandises avec les pays d’Afrique subsaharienne, élargir les livraisons de produits africains sur le marché russe et mettre en place des mécanismes de règlements mutuels utilisant les monnaies nationales. Les commissions intergouvernementales chargées de la coopération commerciale, économique, scientifique et technique avec les pays africains jouent un rôle important dans le renforcement des liens dans les milieux d’affaires. En février 2026, un accord a été signé en vue de la création de la Commission intergouvernementale russo-burkinabè sur la coopération commerciale, économique, scientifique et technique; sa première réunion devrait se tenir d’ici la fin de cette année. La Russie a des atouts à proposer à nos partenaires dans les domaines de l’énergie, de l’exploitation des ressources minérales, de la logistique et des transports, de la mise en place d’infrastructures, ainsi que dans les secteurs de haute technologie, notamment les technologies numériques et l’intelligence artificielle. Nous sommes prêts à partager nos technologies et notre expertise en agronomie et en sélection végétale, dans la production d’engrais, l’irrigation et la pêche. Nous continuons à renforcer la coopération russo-africaine dans les domaines de l’agriculture, de la santé et de la prévention et de la gestion des situations d’urgence. Les laboratoires mobiles russes et les moyens de diagnostic des maladies infectieuses sont très demandés en Afrique. En décembre 2025, un laboratoire mobile du Service fédéral de surveillance de la protection des droits des consommateurs et du bien-être humain (Rospotrebnadzor) a été livré gratuitement au Burkina Faso, et en avril 2026, des formations ont été organisées à l’intention des médecins burkinabè sur la lutte contre les épidémies. Notre pays accorde une grande attention à la jeunesse africaine, en particulier à celle du Burkina Faso. Actuellement, 72 étudiants burkinabè sont inscrits dans des établissements d’enseignement supérieur russes. En 2026, le nombre de places au titre du contingent éducatif attribué au Burkina Faso a été porté à 67. Je tiens à souligner que les établissements d’enseignement russes forment des spécialistes de premier ordre dans tous les domaines de l’économie. Je suis convaincu que le Troisième sommet Russie-Afrique constituera une étape importante dans le partenariat d’égal à égal et tourné vers l’avenir entre la Russie et l’Afrique, ainsi qu’entre la Fédération de Russie et le Burkina Faso, fondé sur le respect mutuel des intérêts de chacun. Igor Martynov Ambassadeur de la Fédération de Russie au Burkina Faso

items.title: La commune de Paris bis
items.description: En mars 1871, lorsque la commune de Paris (gouverne-ment révolutionnaire et insurrectionnel qui a dirigé la France de mars à mai 1871) intervenait, la France était dans un état lamentable après sa défaite face à la Prusse de Otto Von Bismarck en 1870 et la pauvreté qui rongeait le pays. Aussi, l’abolition de l’esclavage intervenue officiellement quelques années plus tôt, avait accentué ce maras-me économique et social, car, la traite du « bois d’ébène » lui permettait de vivre grassement au- dessus de ses moyens réels. En 2026, la situation politique, sociale et écono-mique est quasiment à l’identique, avec l’appau-vrissement avancé des ruraux, la perte d’influence dans son « précarré » qui l’empêche d’équilibrer ses comptes publics et son insertion mécanique dans la mondialisation qui a porté un coup fatal à son secteur industriel. On se retrouve dans une situation où tous les clignotants sont au rouge ; ce qui entraîne une situation insurrectionnelle selon les lois du matéria-lisme historique. Il y aura donc forcément effondre-ment de l’Etat dans sa forme actuelle aussi bien au plan politique et institutionnel (passage à la 6e République ou possiblement avènement d’un gouvernement de salut public) que social avec une réforme obligatoire du système de sécurité sociale qui « bouffe » une part importante de la richesse nationale. Une cure d’amai-grissement qui n’ira pas sans mal, ce qui pousse les officines obscures de l’Hexagone, en rapport avec les esclaves de salon africains, à vouloir déstabiliser coûte que coûte nos Etats pour avoir à nouveau du « gras ». Après l’épisode de ses supplétifs terroristes qui est en passe d’être révolus avec la résolution de nos troupes combattantes et le changement tactique et stratégique sur le théâtre des opérations, la France est passée à une méthode plus soft mais plus dangereuse, à savoir la division et le noyautage au plus haut niveau de nos appareils dirigeants. Le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, n’a pas dit autre chose lors de son adresse à ses frères à l’occasion de la commémoration du 39e anniversaire de l’assassinat de Thomas Sankara, leader de la Révolution d’août 83. « Quand nous sommes divisés, nous ouvrons la porte à l’ennemi », lui facilitant ainsi la tâche dans l’accomplissement de sa sale besogne. Mais, l’adresse du président du Faso prouve que l’appareil dirigeant a pris la mesure de ce nouveau péril qui guette notre processus d’émancipation. Les révolutionnaires de septembre 2022 sont prêts à toutes les éventualités et la France état-sangsue s’il en est, boira le calice jusqu’à la lie. C’est dit. Boubakar SY
