items.title: CAN to citizens: ‘We all, not leaders alone, are guilty’
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, has urged Nigerians to share responsibility for the country’s challenges, including insecurity, corruption and economic hardship, rather than blame political leaders alone. Read Also: DisCos’ revenue rises 450% as debt profile hits N700bn The association called for collective repentance and a renewed commitment to national restoration, saying the Church and citizens must acknowledge their shortcomings and contribute to rebuilding the country. Vice-President of CAN, Rev. Stephen Panya-Baba, stated this in a homily at a special thanksgiving service in Abuja weekend to mark the association’s 50th anniversary, with the theme, “Working Together in Faith.” “The truth, brethren, is that we all stand guilty before God as a Church. This, therefore, requires collective responsibility from all of us to do what is right and support our leaders in the difficult task of rehabilitating and restoring our beloved country,” he said. Panya-Baba said the anniversary provided an opportunity for the Church to reflect on its journey, shortcomings and responsibility to Nigeria’s peace, progress and prosperity. “We have no other country we can call our own. Nigeria is our home, and we have no alternative but to work towards its restoration,” he declared. The CAN vice-president, however, stressed that the association must continue to hold government accountable, noting that speaking truth to power did not mean becoming an opposition party. “CAN has a responsibility to speak truth to power on critical national issues, privately or publicly, as circumstances demand. However, it must never assume the role of an opposition party to the government,” he said. Tracing the association’s origins, Panya-Baba recalled that Christian leaders met in Lagos in August 1976 at the instance of the then Head of State, General Olusegun Obasanjo, and resolved to speak with one voice. He attributed the account to Professor Yusuf Turaki. He said CAN adopted the anniversary theme from the biblical call for unity in John 17:21, with its ecumenical philosophy anchored on unity in essentials, liberty in non-essentials and charity in all things. Panya-Baba said the association had contributed to peacebuilding, the defence of religious freedom, national engagement and public discourse over the past five decades. He also highlighted its support for victims of religious crises and efforts to promote moral values and encourage the participation of women and youths through Women in CAN and Youth in CAN. The cleric acknowledged challenges, including leadership disputes, religious persecution, insecurity, interreligious tensions, financial constraints and public criticism. Despite these difficulties, he urged members to remain united and committed to CAN’s mission. He also appealed to members whose contributions might not be recognised during the anniversary celebrations not to become discouraged. “The journey is not over, and God keeps a much more perfect record,” he said. Panya-Baba paid tribute to past leaders and others who contributed to the association’s growth, while acknowledging the support of its national officers and state and local government structures. He urged Nigerians to examine their individual and collective roles in the country’s difficulties, citing Proverbs 14:34 to emphasise the need for righteousness, repentance and a willingness to confront wrongdoing. The CAN vice-president also called on the association to mobilise Nigerians to pray for the country and seek God’s intervention, while sustaining its advocacy for justice, equity and fairness irrespective of religion, ethnicity or region. items.title: IMF, World Bank hail Oyedele’s G-24 leadership
items.description: By Henry Ojelu Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has received commendation from the leadership of the International Monetary Fund, IMF, and World Bank for his leadership of the Group of 24 (G-24), highlighting Nigeria’s growing voice in global economic discussions. The commendation came during the 2026 IMF and World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, where Oyedele chaired the G-24 Board of Governors meeting and led calls for a fairer global financial system, affordable development financing and faster resolution of sovereign debt crises. IMF Managing Director, Kristalina Georgieva, and World Bank Senior Managing Director, Axel van Trotsenburg, representing World Bank President Ajay Banga, joined other G-24 governors in commending Oyedele’s leadership of discussions on the financing challenges confronting developing economies. The recognition was reinforced by Banga’s meeting with Oyedele and Central Bank of Nigeria Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, during which he acknowledged Nigeria’s reform progress, pointing to private capital inflows that reportedly increased from about $300 million in 2023 to nearly $6 billion in 2026. Oyedele’s performance at the meetings extended beyond diplomatic engagements. As G-24 chairman, he drew attention to the burden of rising debt-servicing costs on developing countries, warning that they were undermining investment, job creation and inclusive growth. A Reuters report quoted him as saying developing economies were paying approximately $500 billion more in debt servicing than developed countries. He urged international financial institutions to provide more accessible and affordable concessional financing to vulnerable economies. The minister also argued against imposing additional tax burdens on vulnerable households and productive sectors amid global economic uncertainty, advocating improved revenue mobilisation. reduced waste and a careful balance between taxation and borrowing. At the Africa’s Golden Future Forum in Bangkok, he also presented Nigeria’s experience with fuel subsidy removal, foreign exchange liberalisation and tax reform as lessons for African countries pursuing sustainable growth. He highlighted cash transfers and education support as measures intended to cushion vulnerable citizens.ing HYPREP’s work and extending environmental remediation to other polluted parts of the region. He described the Ogoni cleanup as a pilot scheme, adding that the committee had involved HYPREP, the Federal Ministry of Environment and other relevant stakeholders in developing the bill. “Very soon, the bill will come up. What we intend to do with that is to sustain what HYPREP is doing and see how it can be taken to all other parts of the Niger Delta,” Dekor said. He commended HYPREP for its commitment to the project, noting that the sites inspected were more than 80 per cent complete. Although the projects were still ongoing, he said the progress recorded was encouraging, expressing confidence that the renewed drive within HYPREP would ensure timely completion and quality delivery. Dekor also praised the project’s skills acquisition component, saying it had equipped young Ogonis with specialised skills sought after internationally. He said about 2,400 youths had been listed among those trained at various centres, adding that the programme would help develop a pool of skilled professionals in Ogoniland. Meanwhile, HYPREP Project Coordinator, Prof. Nenibarini Zabbey, said the project had more than 130 sites across its intervention areas, covering remediation, shoreline cleanup, potable water provision, healthcare improvement and skills development. He said the initiative had created direct and indirect employment opportunities for Ogoni residents, including youths and women. Zabbey highlighted the specialist hospital project, which he said would provide tertiary healthcare services to residents of Ogoni and other people in the region. The facility includes an oncology unit for cancer screening and treatment. He also disclosed that HYPREP had conducted a human health biomonitoring study coordinated by the World Health Organisation’s International Agency for Research on Cancer to examine the relationship between exposure to hydrocarbon contaminants and the health of residents. According to him, the committee’s visit provided an opportunity for lawmakers to assess the projects firsthand and make recommendations to improve the implementation of the cleanup. items.title: Exposition « RUPTURE » : le ministre Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo apprécie la qualité des œuvres
items.description: Le ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, a visité l’exposition « RUPTURE », vendredi 16 octobre 2026, au Musée national de Ouagadougou. Le Musée national du Burkina Faso a organisé l’exposition « RUPTURE », du 18 septembre au 18 octobre 2026. Le ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, l’a visitée, vendredi 16 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Il a rendu hommage au talent des artistes burkinabè et salué la profondeur des œuvres et leur capacité à renouveler sans cesse leur inspiration. Le ministre chargé de la Culture a aussi confié que le thème choisi par les plasticiens cadre avec l’élan national. « Votre thématique est en phase avec la marche du Burkina Faso, avec la vision du Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré », a-t-il soutenu. Au cours de la visite, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, a laissé un message dans le livre d’or du Musée national. « Cette exposition nous donne à voir des œuvres originales, spécialement conçues pour porter un message fort de rupture à tous les niveaux. Elle s’inscrit en droite ligne de la dynamique actuelle de rupture amorcée par la Révolution progressiste populaire portée par le camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, Président du Faso, chef de l’Etat », a-t-il écrit. Le directeur général du Musée national, Sabari Christian Dao, a expliqué que le premier objectif de l’exposition est de rendre justice aux talents locaux. « Il s’agit d’abord de faire comprendre au peuple burkinabè que nos artistes sont très prisés ailleurs. Malheureusement, ils ap-portent la lumière du pays dans le monde entier et ils sont moins connus au niveau national » a-t-il relevé. Il a aussi soutenu que l’exposition vise à porter un message. « Celui de la rupture à tous les niveaux. La rupture dans notre façon de travailler, dans notre façon de réfléchir, dans notre façon de marcher » a-t-il poursuivi. Sabari Christian Dao a, par conséquent, invité ses collaborateurs à rompre avec les anciennes habitudes qui ne sont pas forcément professionnelles. « A partir de cette exposition, nous allons faire du musée un lieu d’excellence. Tout artiste qui aura l’occasion d’exposer ici doit avoir un certain niveau », a-t-il assuré. Plusieurs artistes ont participé à l’exposition. Le sculpteur Siriki Ky, a confié que l’exposition matérialise une rupture à tous les niveaux. « Cette exposition ne ressemble pas aux autres. Même le style de travail, la manière de présenter les œuvres, ce n’est pas comme ce que vous voyez souvent », a-t-il précisé. Julien ZOUNGRANA

items.title: Entrepreneuriat féminin: le gouvernement à l’écoute des promotrices d’unités de transformation
items.description: La ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, le lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kabré et le ministre chargé de l’Industrie, Gnaniodem Serge Poda, ont visité quatre unités de transformation de produits locaux, le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Cette sortie leur a permis de recueillir les préoccupations des entrepreneures et d’explorer les possibilités d’un meilleur accompagnement de leurs initiatives. Le gouvernement entend encourager les femmes qui investissent dans la transformation des produits locaux et mieux cerner leurs difficultés. C’est pourquoi, le ministre chargé de la Famille, le Lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kabré et son collègue du Commerce, Gnaniodem Serge Poda ont effectué une visite conjointe d’entreprises féminines, le vendredi 16 octobre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Cette démarche vise à renforcer la proximité des pouvoirs publics avec les promotrices d’entreprises et à rechercher des solutions pour favoriser le développement de leurs activités. La délégation a débuté sa tournée à « Faso Attiéké », au quartier Zone 1. Sa promotrice, Florence Bassono, s’est réjouie de recevoir les deux membres du gouvernement. « Ils sont venus nous rassurer que nous ne sommes pas seules, qu’ils nous voient, nous suivent et nous accompagnent. Ils sont disposés à faire tout ce qu’ils peuvent, dans le cadre institutionnel, pour nous soutenir », a-t-elle déclaré. En plus de la transformation des produits locaux, l’entreprise mène des initiatives sociales et environnementales. Elle dispose notamment d’une crèche, organise des cours d’alpha-bétisation et participe au traitement des déchets dans le cadre d’une démarche de symbiose industrielle à Loumbila. Sa promotrice a également présenté les emplois créés et les certifications attestant de la qualité et de la sécurité alimentaire de ses produits, notamment les normes NBF (Norme du Burkina Faso) et HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point). Des besoins en équipements et en accompagnement La deuxième étape a conduit les ministres à la Société de transformation des pâtes alimentaires (STPAS), située à Ouaga 2000. Sa promotrice, Safiatou Zongo, a salué cette visite, qu’elle considère comme une occasion d’accroître la visibilité de ses produits. Au quartier Patte d’Oie, c’est l’entreprise Bouda Blandine (EBB), spécialisée dans la production de bière locale, communément appelée dolo qui a reçu la visite des deux ministres. Sa promotrice, Blandine Bouda, est également restauratrice et va-lorise des mets locaux. L’entreprise emploie 12 femmes et propose des produits présentés comme 100 % naturels et certifiés NBF. Pour améliorer les conditions de travail de ses employées et assurer une meilleure conservation de ses produits, Blandine Bouda sollicite des équipements solaires et des systèmes de climatisation. Elle a expliqué que les fortes chaleurs provoquent parfois l’explosion des bou-teilles de dolo, compliquant ainsi le conditionnement et la conservation. La tournée s’est achevée au Laboratoire Odiss Cosmétique, à Pissy. Cette unité transforme des produits forestiers non ligneux et agricoles en cosmétique naturel à forte valeur ajoutée. Sa responsable, Odette Denise Zouré, s’est félicitée de l’intérêt manifesté par les autorités. Structurer les réponses aux préoccupations Au terme de la visite, la ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, le Lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kabré, a salué l’engagement des promotrices et la valeur ajoutée générée par leurs activités. Elle a expliqué que cette sortie conjointe vise à rencontrer des femmes entrepreneures qui peuvent se sentir insuffisamment prises en compte dans les dispositifs d’accompagnement existants. « Nous avons voulu, conjointement avec le ministère de l’Industrie, du Commerce et de l’Artisanat, visiter leurs installations, toucher du doigt leurs réalités et recueillir leurs difficultés et leurs préoccupations afin de voir dans quelle mesure nous pouvons mieux accompagner leurs initiatives », a-t-elle expli-qué. Selon elle, les visites ont permis de mesurer l’engagement des promotrices et de constater la chaîne de valeurs créée par leurs entreprises. Les préoccupations recueillies seront examinées avec le département chargé de l’industrie, du commerce et de l’artisanat afin de mieux structurer les réponses à apporter, a-t-elle promis. Toutefois, Passowendé Pélagie Kabré a précisé que son département n’a pas vocation à financer directement les entreprises privées. Elle a néanmoins assuré que des concertations avec les autres départements concernés pourraient contribuer à créer un environnement favorable au développement de ces initiatives. Enfin, elle a encou-ragé les femmes à s’inspirer des parcours des promotrices rencontrées pour se lancer dans l’entrepreneuriat et la transformation des produits locaux. Adama SAWADOGO

items.title: Electricity: Geometric Power puts Aba ahead of Nigerian cities
items.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chie f For decades, unreliable electricity supply has undermined Nigeria’s industrial growth, forcing businesses to close, driving up production costs and making life increasingly difficult for households. Read Also: D isCos’ revenue rises 450% as debt profile hits N700bn From textile mills in Kaduna, Kano, Lagos and Onitsha to vehicle assembly plants, tyre factories and footwear manufacturers, several once-thriving industries have struggled or shut down, partly because of inadequate power supply. Now in Aba, Abia State, a different experience is emerging, as the Geometric Power-owned Aba Power distribution network provides electricity to businesses, institutions and households, enabling some to reduce dependence on costly petrol and diesel generators. The development is reshaping business operations in the commercial hub, with manufacturers reporting uninterrupted production, traders extending working hours and households enjoying improved food preservation and lower running costs. Geometric Power Chairman, Professor Barth Nnaji, described the Aba Integrated Power Project, an investment exceeding $900 million, as a dream come true. He said the company was committed to providing reliable and affordable electricity to customers, irrespective of their social or economic status. “Our services are for all people, regardless of class or status. Electricity is a fundamental right of the Nigerian people, and we are happy to provide reliable and affordable electricity to all our customers,” Nnaji said. He added that, unlike other legacy distribution companies, Aba Power was wholly privately owned and had not received Federal Government subsidies. Role of Afreximbank The decision of the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) to provide a $50 million facility to Geometric Power Limited after a seven-year delay was what made Aba Power a reality today. The Group Managing Director of Geometric Power, Mrs. Agatha Nnaji, said the bank provided the lifeline that enabled the project to be commissioned, saying, “Afreximbank is the bank that provided the funding that enabled us to complete and commission the project.” “As you may know, politics got in the way, human error impacted the project, and it was delayed just as we were about to commission it. So, for seven years, we were simply maintaining the facilities that were already in place. We had staff who had to be paid to keep maintaining them. “Eventually, when we determined the exact amount needed to complete the project—after President Jonathan intervened and his successor, the late President Muhammadu Buhari, directed his team to resolve the issues arising from the privatization—we were thrilled that Afreximbank stepped in. They shared our vision and understood the impact the project would have on the community. “I believe that was the turning point for them. Seeing Aba’s potential as an industrial hub in Africa made them far more willing to find a way to make the project work. Although subsequent challenges prolonged completion, Afreximbank ultimately came to the rescue. “At that crucial juncture, we needed $50 million, and they provided it. Honestly, Afreximbank’s role in all of this was remarkable. Ordinarily, a bank or financier would walk away from a project facing the kinds of hurdles we had at the time. “We were operating in an environment where the government had breached the terms of our signed agreement. We were dealing with civil and public service officials who knew what needed to be done but refused to act. “There was little to offer them comfort beyond the sheer determination of our lead investor. For him, it wasn’t merely a financial venture; his drive to see the project through was fueled by a desire to create a lasting, positive impact on people’s lives.” Infrastructure built for reliability The company says its investment in distribution infrastructure is central to its efforts to maintain stable electricity supply. According to the Director of Commercial Operations, Engineer Victor Ngwoke, Aba Power deliberately invested in heavy-duty tubular steel poles designed to withstand extreme conditions and minimise disruptions. “We wanted to have a very sturdy and reliable infrastructure. We, therefore, deliberately invested in heavy tubular steel poles,” he said. Ngwoke explained that the poles have deeply buried concrete foundations and are designed to withstand substantial impact, including collisions with vehicles. He said the company also maintained standards for conventional concrete poles and worked to restore damaged infrastructure quickly whenever faults occurred. On metering, the director said approximately 98 per cent of Aba Power’s customers had prepaid meters, helping to reduce disputes associated with estimated billing. With prepaid meters, customers can monitor their consumption and manage electricity expenses more effectively. Ngwoke also disclosed that the company deployed smart meters and monitoring teams to detect and prevent electricity theft, including illegal connections and meter bypasses. He said residents had also supported efforts to protect the network, recognising the benefits of reliable electricity to their businesses and livelihoods. Excess capacity, wider reach Aba Power currently takes an average of 50 to 60 megawatts from an installed generation capacity exceeding 140MW, according to the company. The available capacity has enabled it to extend electricity supply to parts of neighbouring Rivers State, where some communities are underserved by the Port Harcourt Electricity Distribution Company. The company says it hopes to extend its reach across Abia State, subject to the necessary infrastructure and operational requirements. Polytechnic cuts energy costs by 80% One of the institutions benefiting from the improved supply is Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, whose Rector, Professor Christopher Okoro, said the development had transformed academic and administrative activities. Okoro, who assumed office in 2024, said one of the first challenges he encountered was a huge outstanding diesel bill, which he considered unsustainable. He contacted Nnaji for assistance, and the institution was connected to Aba Power within 48 hours. Before the connection, he said, academic activities, research and other operations were constrained by unreliable electricity, with staff often leaving the campus by 2pm. With the improved supply, students and staff now remain on campus until late in the evening, despite the institution not being residential. “Before now, staff used to leave by 2pm. They cannot work without electricity. You cannot carry out research without electricity,” he said. The rector said the institution’s energy costs had fallen by about 80 per cent. Manufacturers, traders extend working hours At Damson Industries, a manufacturer of shoe components, Chairman David Mmadueke, said reliable electricity had enabled the company to operate day and night shifts without routinely shutting down because of power outages. “We have light here morning and night. The only time we didn’t have light was when the company had a problem with gas supply for about three days. Apart from that, this factory has never closed because there is no electricity,” he said. Similarly, the President of Aba North Shoe Plaza, Obioma Onyebuchi, said the plaza, which houses more than 2,000 shops, switched to Aba Power on January 14 and had since enjoyed steady supply. According to him, traders no longer depend on individual petrol or diesel generators, as the company has ensured that customers are metered. “With the constant electricity supply from Aba Power, we can now work throughout the day. This has increased the productivity of our members,” he said. Although some traders consider the electricity tariff high, Onyebuchi said the cost remained preferable to the substantial sums previously spent on fuel. He expressed the plaza’s readiness to support the company to sustain reliable supply. Steady power eases household expenses Beyond factories and commercial centres, improved electricity supply is also changing how some households manage their finances. Mrs Ada-Ngizi Greg-Ilobinso, a wife, mother and teacher, said reliable electricity had made household management easier, particularly in food storage and budgeting. She explained that she could now purchase food items in bulk, preserve them in a freezer and reduce the frequency of shopping trips. “Aba Power has really affected my life positively in so many ways. As a mother and a wife, and also as a housekeeper, a house manager, if I may say, it has really helped me because now we have steady light,” she said. While the experiences of residents, manufacturers and institutions point to significant gains, the wider impact will depend on the consistency, affordability and reach of the electricity service. Vanguard News The post Electricity: Geometric Power puts Aba ahead of Nigerian cities appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pour l’intérêt des peuples
items.description: La Confédération des Etats du Sahel (AES) et la Communauté économique des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (CEDEAO) ont ouvert, le 17 octobre 2026, à Dakar au Sénégal, une nouvelle page de leurs relations. La rencontre de Dakar marque une étape importante dans la recherche d’un cadre de coopération entre les deux organisations sous régionales. Au-delà des divergences politiques et institutionnelles, le conclave traduit un impératif de préserver les intérêts des peuples ouest-africains. Il s’agit là d’une initiative diplomatique à saluer à sa juste valeur. En effet, dans les relations entre Etats, le recours aux négociations n’est pas un aveu de faiblesse. Il est plutôt une manifestation de maturité politique, de lucidité et de responsabilité. Lorsque des décisions institutionnelles engagent l’avenir de millions de citoyens, le dialogue demeure un instrument essentiel pour prévenir des ruptures préjudiciables, désamorcer d’éventuelles tensions et rechercher des solutions mutuellement bénéfiques. L’ouverture de ces échanges consacre également la reconnaissance d’une réalité politique désormais indiscutable. Il s’agit de l’existence de deux regroupements géographiques dans l’espace ouest-africain. D’un côté, la CEDEAO et de l’autre, la Confédération AES, constituée par le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger. Prendre acte de cette réalité revient simplement à entretenir une cohabitation fructueuse et à faciliter le dialogue. Cette donne ne signifie ni renoncer à ses convictions, ni renier ses choix souverains. Au contraire, elle consiste à se donner les moyens de construire des relations fondées sur le respect mutuel, la considération des intérêts réciproques, la recherche de solutions pragmatiques… Cela est d’autant plus indispensable que les enjeux sont considérables. Ils touchent d’abord à la libre circulation des personnes et des biens, à la sécurité juridique des ressortissants établis de part et d’autre des frontières, ainsi qu’à la préservation des liens familiaux, sociaux et économiques. Ils concernent ensuite la continuité des échanges commerciaux et des approvision-nements, notamment en denrées alimentaires, en hydrocarbures et autres produits agricoles. Pour des pays sahéliens, l’accès aux corridors portuaires des pays côtiers demeure capital. De même, les pays côtiers tirent de leurs échanges avec les pays sahéliens des revenus substantiels issus du transit des marchandises, des activités portuaires, du transport, de la logistique et du commerce, tout en consolidant leurs marchés et leurs débouchés économiques. La fluidité des échanges entre les deux entités profite ainsi à l’ensemble des acteurs de la sous-région. La sécurité constitue un autre défi majeur. Face aux menaces terroristes et criminelles qui ignorent les frontières, la coopération, le partage d’informations et le maintien de canaux de communication opérationnels doivent prévaloir sur les incompréhensions politiques. La protection des populations exige des réponses coordonnées, pragmatiques et adaptées aux réalités du terrain. A cela s’ajoute la nécessité de clarifier les relations juridiques et institutionnelles entre les deux espaces, afin d’éviter les incertitudes susceptibles de fragiliser les échanges et les droits des citoyens. La poursuite des négociations, dans un esprit de franchise et de respect, sera déterminante pour consolider la confiance et prévenir les conséquences d’une fragmentation durable de l’espace ouest-africain. La rencontre de Dakar rappelle déjà une vérité fondamentale qui est que la souveraineté et la coopération ne sont pas antinomiques. Lorsqu’elles s’exercent dans la prise en compte des intérêts légitimes de chacun, elles peuvent se renforcer réciproquement. L’avenir de notre sous-région ne se construira ni dans l’immobilisme ni dans la confrontation permanente, mais dans la capacité des dirigeants à dialoguer sans forcément renoncer à leurs principes et à rechercher, avec détermination, des solutions profitables à leurs peuples. C’est à cette exigence de responsabilité historique que les échanges de Dakar invitent désormais l’ensemble des acteurs ouest-africains. Par Assetou BADOH

items.title: Audience du Président du Faso: le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré confie une mission aux Etoiles du Faso
items.description: Le Président du Faso, chef de l’Etat, le camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a échangé, vendredi dans la matinée avec les Etoiles du Faso, des Ambassadeurs du civisme et les lauréats du Grand prix d’engagement citoyen. Le chef de l’Etat a félicité ces illustres élus avant de les envoyer en mission qu’ils sont condamnés à réussir : « promouvoir le civisme, le patriotisme et que leur brillance se déteigne sur les autres Burkinabè ». Les hôtes du président du Faso à cette audience sont de trois catégories : les Etoiles du Faso, des personnalités modèles dans leurs domaines d’activités, les Ambassadeurs du civisme qui sont des élèves lauréats du concours sur le civisme, et les lauréats du Grand prix d’engagement citoyen décerné à des personnalités modèles qui ont fait flotter le pavillon national. Conduits par le ministre de la Justice, camarade Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, ces femmes et hommes de différentes générations se voient confiées une mission par le Président du Faso, chef de l’Etat, le camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. « Vous êtes condamnés à être des Etoiles pour toujours, pour illuminer le cerveau des plus jeunes et de tous vos frères. Donc, c’est une mission qui vous est confiée désormais de pouvoir illuminer tout un chacun », a-t-il dit aux Etoiles avant de s’adresser aux Ambassadeurs : « Vous avez aussi une grosse mission. Et vous aussi, vous n’avez pas le droit à l’erreur de votre jeune âge ». Le président du Faso, a également expliqué à ces « élus », la quintessence du civisme et du patriotisme, qui sont des valeurs fondamentales et un socle du développement. Pour le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le patriotisme, c’est « l’amour que nous avons pour notre chère Patrie, l’amour que nous avons pour la terre que nos ancêtres se sont battus pour nous léguer, l’amour que nous avons à entretenir cette terre pour la remettre dans de meilleures conditions à nos enfants, aux générations à venir. L’amour que nous avons entre nous, citoyens du même pays, entre nos frères et sœurs. Nous devons aimer tout Burkinabè comme notre sang ». Cette audience se tenant dans le cadre des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne dont le thème porte sur la promotion du consommer local, le chef de l’Etat, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a expliqué à ses hôtes, les enjeux. « L’enfant intelligent achète les galettes de sa maman. Encore faut-il que la maman puisse produire ses galettes et que l’enfant intelligent les paie ? Mais ça veut dire beaucoup de choses. Pour faire des galettes, il faut qu’on produise. Voilà pourquoi partout où nous sommes, il faut qu’on arrive à produire ce dont on a besoin. Nous ne pouvons pas dire qu’on est patriote et continuer d’importer ce que nous pouvons produire nous-mêmes ici », a fait comprendre le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Le Porte-parole des Etoiles, le camarade Inoussa Saré, a remercié le président du Faso pour l’honneur et a traduit l’engagement de tous les lauréats aux côtés du capitaine Ibrahim Traoré pour relever les défis. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: Montenegrin PM meets Chinese FM
items.description: Montenegrin Prime Minister Milojko Spajic met with visiting Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Podgorica on Sunday. Both sides expressed willingness to further deepen bilateral relations and expand practical cooperation. Spajic asked Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, to convey his sincere greetings to Chinese leaders. Recalling the warm reception he received during his visit to China in June, Spajic said Wang's visit demonstrates the importance China attaches to bilateral relations. Montenegro and China share historical memories and traditional friendship, as both countries fought against fascism and foreign aggression during World War II, he said. Montenegro highly values China's status and influence as a major country and appreciates China's responsible efforts to curb rising global oil prices amid the conflicts in the Middle East, which have helped Montenegro and other small and medium-sized countries cope with the energy crisis, demonstrating China's sense of responsibility as a major country, Spajic said. Noting Montenegro's sound economic and social development in recent years, Spajic said Chinese enterprises have helped the country complete the construction of its north-south expressway. The ongoing joint restoration of the Tara River Bridge is a project of great historical significance, bringing the two peoples closer and serving as a testament to their traditional friendship, he said. China has always been one of Montenegro's most important partners in its development, Spajic said, adding that deepening cooperation with China meets the aspirations of the Montenegrin people and enjoys broad public support. Montenegro stands ready to work closely with China to advance cooperation in tourism, infrastructure and green transition, engage in exchanges of experience in governance and accelerate their respective development and revitalization, he said. Spajic welcomed the new consensus reached through the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, saying that closer communication and cooperation between China and the EU, as close partners and two major global forces and markets, are conducive to global stability and development. Wang conveyed Chinese leaders' best wishes to Spajic, saying that China and Montenegro have always been good friends on their paths toward development and revitalization. The two countries have respected and supported each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns, providing an important guarantee for the sound and steady development of bilateral relations, he said. Noting that the 20th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations marks an important year for building on the past and paving the way for the future, Wang said China stands ready to explore with Montenegro ways to elevate bilateral relations to a higher level, deepen exchanges and cooperation across various fields, and become long-term and trustworthy strategic partners. Wang said China and Montenegro share much in common. Both peoples are unafraid of bullying and firmly defend their national dignity. They both achieved victory in the World Anti-Fascist War and should remain vigilant against the resurgence of militarism. Both countries uphold and practice multilateralism and oppose a return to the "law of the jungle," he said. Both countries advocate economic globalization, safeguard free trade and oppose all forms of conservatism and isolationism, Wang said, adding that both support resolving disputes through dialogue and peaceful political means. The Tara River Bridge, he said, connects the hearts of the two peoples and carries both the history and future of bilateral relations. China's assistance in restoring the bridge is of great historical and social significance, he added. Wang said China understands Montenegro's efforts to join the EU and believes that its EU accession process is fully compatible with strengthening ties with China, expressing hope that Montenegro will inject fresh impetus into the health development of China-EU relations.

items.title: DisCos’ revenue rises 450% as debt profile hits N700bn
items.description: *Supply grows by 4.8% *Available plant capacity falls by 41% *13 years of privatisation yield little results *FG turns to bonds to tackle N6trn debt *Power supply has improved, Power Minister insists *Consumers, experts react Revenue collected by Nigeria’s electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) rose by about 450 per cent in eight years, from N218.16 billion in the first half of 2018 to N1.2 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026, far outpacing growth in electricity supply over the period. Read Also: NLC, Falana, activists rally Nigerians against petrol price hike, hardship Data from the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), analysed by Financial Vanguard, showed that while DisCos’ revenue increased by about N983.04 billion, total electricity supply grew by only 4.8 per cent, from 16,861 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in the first half of 2018 to 17,668GWh in the first half of 2026, even as their debt profile in the last six months hits N700billion. The data also indicated that average available generation capacity declined by 41 per cent, from 7,565.5 megawatts (MW) in the first half of 2018 to 4,456MW in the corresponding period of 2026. On an annual basis, DisCos’ revenue increased by about 666 per cent in ten years, from N302.93 billion in 2016 to N2.32 trillion in 2025, highlighting the widening gap between revenue growth and improvements in electricity supply. NERC data showed that while DisCos’ annual revenue rose by about N2.016 trillion over the period, average daily power generation increased by approximately 36 per cent, from 3,276MW in 2016 to 4,475MW in 2025. The disparity has raised concerns about the extent to which increased revenue collections have translated into improved electricity supply and service delivery to consumers, 13 years after the privatisation of the power sector. In the same vein, data from NERC showed that in the first half of 2026, DisCos failed to collect N700.53 billion. It indicated that while the utilities received N1.9trillion worth of energy from the market, they collected N1.2trillion from consumers, leaving a balance of N700 billion. The Rural Electrification Agency (REA) has estimated that about 85 million Nigerians still lack access to electricity. In 2016, DisCos collected N302.925 billion, while total annual electricity supply stood at 23,742GWh. By 2025, revenue had risen by about 666 per cent to N2.3188 trillion, while annual electricity supply increased by 31.6 per cent to 31,251GWh. DisCos’ revenue rose to N370.456 billion in 2017, before increasing to N448.749 billion in 2019 and N542.729 billion in 2020. Collections further climbed to N775.336 billion in 2021 and N841.811 billion in 2022. The upward trend accelerated in subsequent years, with revenue reaching N1.0775 trillion in 2023, N1.6597 trillion in 2024 and N2.3188 trillion in 2025. By comparison, annual electricity supply increased from 23,742GWh in 2016 to 33,489.17GWh in 2019 and 35,242.17GWh in 2020. It rose further to 36,710.60GWh in 2023 and peaked at 37,093.70GWh in 2024 before declining to 31,251GWh in 2025. The divergence was particularly evident in 2025, when annual electricity supply fell by about 15.7 per cent from 37,093.70GWh in 2024, even as DisCos’ revenue increased from N1.6597 trillion to N2.3188 trillion. 13 years of privatisation yield little results The bulk of the power sector was privatised in November 2013, with generation plants and 11 distribution companies handed over to private investors, while the Federal Government retained control of the transmission segment. The arrangement formed the basis of the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry, NESI. However, 13 years after privatisation, concerns remain over the pace of growth in electricity supply despite over N10 trillion public investment in the sector. NERC data showed that in 2016, three years after privatisation, the average available generation capacity of 27 power plants was 7,527MW, while actual average generation stood at 3,276MW. By 2025, with installed generation capacity of more than 13,000MW, average available capacity had fallen by 28.3 per cent to 5,398MW, while average generation rose to 4,475MW. FG turns to bonds to tackle N6trn debt With the Federal Government’s debts to power generation companies hitting the N6 trillion mark at the end of 2025, the government has gone to the bond market to raise funds to make up for its inability to fund electricity subsidies from the national budget. NERC, in its 2025 industry report, put the Federal Government’s gross tariff subsidy obligation at N1.928 trillion for the year, representing 57.44 percent of the total NBET invoice. The amount translates to an average subsidy obligation of N160.69 billion per month. The government’s subsidy obligation was distributed across the four quarters, with N536.40 billion recorded in the first quarter, N514.36 billion in the second quarter, N458.76 billion in the third quarter and N418.79 billion in the fourth quarter. The 2025 figure represented a slight decline from the N1.949 trillion subsidy obligation recorded in 2024. The government had in September 2026 signed the N728.979 billion Series 2 bond under its N4 trillion Power Sector Debt Reduction Programme, in a fresh move to settle verified legacy debts owed to electricity generation companies and restore liquidity to Nigeria’s power sector. The transaction comprised N402 billion in cash bonds raised from the domestic capital market and N326.979 billion in non-cash bonds allotted to participating generation companies. The Managing Director/CEO, Nigerian Bulk Electricity Trading Plc, Akin Odeyemi said, at the backdrop of weak growth in power supply the GenCos appear to be shackled by indebtedness by the Federal Government with outstanding debt put around N6 trillion at the beginning of this year. Consequently, the government had in September 2026 signed the N728.979 billion Series 2 bond under its N4 trillion Power Sector Debt Reduction Programme, in a fresh move to settle verified legacy debts owed to electricity generation companies and restore liquidity to Nigeria’s power sector. The transaction comprised N402 billion in cash bonds raised from the domestic capital market and N326.979 billion in non-cash bonds allotted to participating generation companies. Odeyemi said at the weekend that NBET has commenced the settlement of participating Generation Companies (GenCos) and their associated Gas Companies following the successful issuance and signing of the N728.979 billion Series 2 Bonds under the N4 trillion Power Sector Multi-Instrument Issuance Programme. He noted that the milestone “represents a significant step in the implementation of the Presidential Power Sector Debt Reduction Programme, under the visionary leadership of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and in furtherance of the objectives of the Renewed Hope Agenda. “The settlement is being undertaken through a combination of N402,000,000,000.00 in Cash Bonds and N326,979,000,000.00 in Non-Cash Bonds, in accordance with the approved settlement framework”, he added. Power supply has improved, Power Minister insists Despite concerns over the sector’s performance, the Minister of Power, Mr. Joseph Tegbe, has insisted that electricity supply has improved over the past three months. Tegbe, who acknowledged that some parts of the country continued to experience poor supply, said the government was working to address the challenges. According to him, “Operational record reports show generation and transmission above 5,000MW over the past couple of weeks, compared to the 3,700 to 4,700MW range before June, and a generation peak of 5,330MW during August and September. “Our next task is to sustain these gains and translate them into more dependable supply at customer level. We are aware that a national peak alone cannot describe the experience of every community.” He said the government’s efforts to address the challenges were anchored on three pillars: stabilising the value chain, restoring market discipline and strengthening governance. “Under the first pillar, the 375MW Alaoji open-cycle power plant was restored to the national grid after three years offline. “A number of substations have been upgraded. For instance, new transformers have been commissioned at Apapa, Ijora, Alausa and Lekki in Lagos, unlocking 672MW of transmission capacity, while a new 300MVA transformer has been energised at Katampe in Abuja, unlocking another 240MW of transmission capacity. “These interventions restored existing assets and strengthened the network serving major centres of demand.” The Minister said the government was also working to diversify the country’s energy mix, with emphasis on solar power. He said the completed electrification portfolio under the REA and its partners comprised 62 solar and mini-grid installations across 30 states, representing about 43.6MW of installed solar capacity and 41,735 new connections, with an estimated reach of more than 208,000 people. Reform remains unfinished — Babalola Speaking on the state of the power sector, Special Adviser to the President on Power and Chairman, Presidential Task Force on Power Sector Reset and Restoration, Dr. Lanre Babalola, said the reforms initiated by the government remained incomplete. Babalola noted that Nigeria’s electricity challenge was not simply a lack of generation capacity. “Our deeper problem is that we have not yet built a system capable of consistently converting available capacity into reliable electricity, commercial value and sustainable investment,” he said. According to him, “We must also recognise that Nigeria’s electricity reform remains an unfinished transition. “We unbundled the old vertically integrated utility. Generation and distribution assets were privatised. A bulk trader was established. And we expected private capital and commercial discipline to progressively transform the industry. “But we never fully completed the transition to the competitive electricity market envisaged by those reforms. “The single-buyer model was conceived as a transitional mechanism. NBET provided a credible intermediary while market participants developed the creditworthiness required for direct contracting. “But a transitional mechanism becomes a structural constraint if the transition never happens. The objective cannot be to preserve the institutions of transition indefinitely. The objective must be to complete the transition.” ‘Nigerians have been paying for darkness’ — Fadipe Reacting to the figures, lawyer and Lead Consultant at Sage Consulting on Power Sector, Mr. Bode Fadipe, said the data raised questions about whether consumers had received commensurate value for the money paid for electricity. “What this data has just confirmed is that Nigerians have been paying for darkness,” Fadipe said. He identified inadequate investment as one of the major challenges responsible for the limited improvement in electricity supply, arguing that the figures also justified NERC’s directive requiring DisCos to retain part of their revenue for investment. “You will recall that the DisCos vehemently protested this order, but NERC thankfully insisted on the implementation of the order,” he said. Fadipe, however, said the level of compliance with the investment directive remained a separate issue that needed to be established. He called for closer monitoring of DisCos and strict enforcement of NERC’s investment directives. “NERC must dutifully enforce its order on investment. NERC must also set timelines for certain levels of improvement,” he said. He further advocated forensic audits of investments by DisCos to determine whether funds earmarked for infrastructure were being properly utilised, while urging NERC to work with market participants on debt recovery. Consumers demand stronger protection Also reacting, consumer rights advocate and Executive Director, Electricity Consumer Protection Advocacy Centre, Chief Princewill Okorie, said the revenue figures raised questions about the quality of service delivered to consumers. Okorie said the decentralisation of the electricity sector under the new legal framework had brought regulation closer to consumers in the states, but argued that enforcement of consumer protection provisions remained a major challenge. According to him, consumers continued to face issues including estimated billing, infrastructure charges and alleged non-compliance with regulatory directives. He alleged that in some communities, consumers had been compelled to contribute money for transformers and other distribution infrastructure despite regulatory obligations on DisCos. “Consumers are not paying” has often been cited as a reason for poor service, Okorie said, but argued that the quality and basis of bills issued to consumers must also be examined. “The appropriate question to ask is: how did they generate these bills? Were they justifiably, accountably and transparently generated?” he said. He called for stronger enforcement of electricity regulations and greater protection for consumers, particularly in rural communities. Okorie also advocated a dedicated mechanism for investigating alleged electricity-related violations and improving consumer awareness of their rights. He questioned why the Federal Ministry of Power did not have a dedicated consumer protection unit and urged stronger involvement by consumer protection authorities in educating electricity users about their rights. He also questioned claims that the Federal Government was paying subsidies in the sector, noting that electricity consumers provide much of the equipment used by DisCos, including poles, cables and transformers, without reimbursement from the utilities. items.title: Mali : Aïssatou Sinko Diallo invite le président Doumbouya à visiter la préfecture et plaide pour son titre de citoyen d’honneur
items.description: Mali, Guinée – Ancienne présidente de la délégation spéciale de Mali, Aïssatou Sinko Diallo salue les actions de développement engagées par le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, en faveur de la préfecture de Mali. À travers une démarche empreinte de reconnaissance et d’attachement à sa communauté, elle exprime le souhait de voir le chef de l’État effectuer une visite dans cette localité du Fouta-Djalon et recevoir le titre de citoyen d’honneur de la préfecture, en reconnaissance des efforts consentis pour son développement. Pour cette femme engagée dans la vie publique et profondément attachée aux aspirations de ses concitoyens, les projets en cours constituent des avancées importantes pour l’avenir de Mali. Parmi les initiatives qui retiennent particulièrement son attention figurent les travaux de la route Labé-Mali, la reconstruction de la grande mosquée ainsi que les différents projets d’infrastructures destinés à améliorer les conditions de vie des populations. Aïssatou Sinko Diallo, une femme attachée au développement de sa préfecture Forte de son expérience à la tête de la délégation spéciale de Mali, Aïssatou Sinko Diallo demeure attentive aux préoccupations des populations et aux perspectives de développement de sa préfecture. Son engagement témoigne de sa volonté de voir Mali bénéficier pleinement des politiques publiques et des investissements susceptibles de transformer durablement son quotidien. À ses yeux, le développement d'une localité repose sur des infrastructures de qualité, mais également sur l'écoute des citoyens, la promotion des initiatives locales et la prise en compte des aspirations des femmes et des jeunes. C'est dans cet esprit qu'elle apprécie les projets engagés sous le leadership du président Mamadi Doumbouya, qu'elle considère comme des leviers importants pour renforcer l'accessibilité de la préfecture, stimuler les activités économiques et ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives aux communautés locales. Une invitation officielle souhaitée au président de la République Au regard de ces réalisations, Aïssatou Sinko Diallo souhaite vivement que le président de la République effectue une visite à Mali. Une telle présence constituerait, selon elle, une occasion privilégiée de découvrir les réalités de la préfecture, de constater les avancées enregistrées et d'échanger directement avec les populations sur leurs attentes et leurs priorités. Elle souhaite également que les autorités et les instances compétentes puissent envisager l'attribution à Mamadi Doumbouya du titre de citoyen d'honneur de la préfecture de Mali. Pour elle, cette distinction représenterait un geste symbolique fort, traduisant la reconnaissance des populations à l'égard des efforts de développement dont leur territoire bénéficie. Au-delà du titre, cette initiative exprime surtout son attachement à une relation de proximité entre les dirigeants et les citoyens. La promotion des femmes, un engagement au cœur de sa vision L'engagement d'Aïssatou Sinko Diallo ne se limite pas aux questions d'infrastructures. Elle accorde également une importance particulière à la place des femmes dans le développement de la Guinée. Convaincue que les femmes constituent une force essentielle pour la transformation économique et sociale du pays, elle souhaite voir leurs initiatives davantage soutenues, leur autonomisation renforcée et leur participation à la prise de décision encouragée. À travers cette vision, elle défend une approche du développement dans laquelle les femmes, les jeunes et l'ensemble des composantes de la société trouvent leur place et contribuent activement à la construction d'une Guinée plus prospère. Son parcours à la tête de la délégation spéciale de Mali lui a permis de côtoyer les réalités locales et de mieux comprendre les attentes des populations. Cette expérience nourrit aujourd'hui son attachement aux questions de gouvernance locale, de développement territorial et de participation citoyenne. Mali, une préfecture tournée vers de nouvelles perspectives En mettant en avant les actions entreprises en faveur de Mali, Aïssatou Sinko Diallo entend porter un message de reconnaissance, tout en encourageant la poursuite des efforts engagés pour le développement de la préfecture. Son souhait est clair : voir les chantiers se poursuivre, les infrastructures se renforcer et les populations bénéficier concrètement des investissements réalisés. À travers son appel au président Mamadi Doumbouya, elle exprime une ambition qui dépasse le simple constat des réalisations : celle de voir Mali devenir un territoire plus accessible, plus dynamique et davantage tourné vers l'avenir. Pour Aïssatou Sinko Diallo, la reconnaissance des actions publiques, la promotion des femmes et la défense des intérêts des populations doivent rester au cœur de toute démarche visant à faire avancer la préfecture de Mali et, plus largement, la Guinée. L’article Mali : Aïssatou Sinko Diallo invite le président Doumbouya à visiter la préfecture et plaide pour son titre de citoyen d’honneur est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Audience du Président du Faso: les DG des Douanes de l’ AES et du Togo rendent compte au chef de l’Etat
items.description: Le Président du Faso, chef de l’Etat, Président en exercice de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel, le camarade capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a reçu en audience, vendredi matin, une délégation des directeurs généraux des douanes des pays membres de la Confédération AES et du Togo. Conduite par la ministre déléguée chargée du Budget, camarade Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, la délégation est venue faire, au président en exercice de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel, le point sur la rencontre des directeurs généraux des douanes de la confédération et du commissaire général de l’Office togolais des Recettes qui s’est tenue le 15 octobre dernier à Ouagadougou. « Il s’agit d’examiner les recommandations de la dernière réunion de Bamako (…), de compléter le texte devant créer l’union douanière, d’instituer les procédures de certification et de reconnaissance de l’origine confédérale. Nous avons pu valider le projet de décision en la matière. Et avec l’administration des douanes du Togo nous avons fait l’état de mise œuvre de l’interconnexion de nos systèmes informatifs », a soutenu le porte-parole de la délégation, le directeur général des douanes du Niger, le colonel Mohamed Yacouba Sido, qui confie que la délégation a reçu des orientations du chef de l’Etat en matière de facilitation du commerce: « le président du Faso nous a instruits de mettre en œuvre tous les instruments nécessaires afin de faciliter les échanges entre nos Etats ». Selon le commissaire des douanes et droits indirects de l’Office togolais des Recettes, le colonel des douanes Konzi TEÏ, le président du Faso a également donné des orientations pour le renforcement du rôle des douanes dans l’économie qu’il faut assainir. « Les orientations du chef de l’Etat vont être pour nous un testament dans la suite de la coopération entre les douanes togolaises de l’OTR et les Etats de la Confédération AES », a-t-il précisé. items.title: Bayt Mal Al-Qods présente son bilan devant l’OCI
items.description: L’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif, bras exécutif du Comité Al-Qods présidé par le Roi Mohammed VI, a remis samedi à Baghdad, aux délégations des États membres de l’Organisation de la Coopération Islamique (OCI) participant à la 52e session du Conseil des ministres des Affaires étrangères de ladite Organisation, un rapport sur le bilan de ses actions humanitaires dans la Ville sainte. Ce rapport comprend des dépliants et des supports visuels présentant les réalisations de l’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif entre juin 2025 et septembre 2026, ainsi qu’une note de présentation de son approche, axée sur la complémentarité entre les interventions humanitaires directes et les programmes d’autonomisation sociale et économique. Il présente également les grandes lignes de la vision de l'Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif à l’horizon 2030, élaborée en partenariat avec les institutions et les acteurs de la société civile palestinienne, sous le slogan « La durabilité dans la planification et l’action ». Le rapport indique que l’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif a tenu en septembre dernier, une série de consultations dans la Ville Sainte et à Ramallah afin d’élaborer son programme d’action pour la période 2027-2030, articulé autour de trois axes stratégiques portant sur le renforcement de la gouvernance administrative et la numérisation, l’amélioration des ressources de l’Agence et la diversification de ses sources de financement, ainsi que la mise en place d’un plan d’action intégré en faveur des secteurs sociaux. Ce programme d’action pour la période 2027-2030 s'articule autour de dix programmes combinant la poursuite des interventions de base de l’Agence et le développement de nouveaux domaines d’action adaptés aux mutations sociales, économiques et technologiques, selon une architecture financière fondée sur un seuil de sécurité annuel de 7 millions de dollars, auquel s’ajouteront les ressources supplémentaires que l’institution sera en mesure de mobiliser dans le cadre des solutions proposées par le plan, souligne le rapport. S’agissant du bilan des interventions de l'Agence au cours de l’année 2026, le rapport met en avant la diversité de ses programmes dans les domaines de l’action sociale, de l’éducation, de la santé, de l’autonomisation économique et de l’agriculture, avec un accent mis également sur les initiatives destinées aux enfants et aux jeunes, les activités culturelles et académiques et les programmes d’innovation. Sur le plan social, le programme d’aide du Ramadan 1447 de l’Hégire a notamment porté sur la distribution de 5.000 paniers alimentaires, la fourniture de 20.000 repas d’iftar par jour, la remise de vêtements de l’Aïd Al-Fitr à 500 orphelins et la distribution de 5.112 bons d’achat. L’Agence a également mis en œuvre l’initiative « Un hiver chaud », au profit de 120 ménages réparties dans 12 communautés bédouines au sud-est de la ville. Dans le secteur de l’éducation, l’Agence a apporté son soutien à plusieurs établissements scolaires dans les communautés bédouines d’Al-Qods en leur fournissant des équipements et du matériel pédagogique, outre la distribution de 3.000 cartables ainsi que des fournitures scolaires au titre de l’année scolaire 2026-2027. Ces actions ont été complétées par des initiatives éducatives destinées aux enfants hospitalisés à l’hôpital Al-Matlaa, ainsi que par un programme d’écoles d’été ayant bénéficié à plus de 3.000 enfants dans une vingtaine d’établissements et de centres. Dans le cadre du développement de ces interventions, l’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif a lancé, mi-juillet dernier, un programme intégré de soutien à l’éducation et à la formation à Al-Qods pour la période 2027-2030, qui se veut la continuité de son précédent programme dans ce domaine. Ce dispositif repose sur quatre axes portant sur l’amélioration et la réhabilitation de l’environnement scolaire, l’élargissement des bourses d’études et des stages de formation, le soutien à l’entrepreneuriat et aux technologies numériques, ainsi que le renforcement des activités parascolaires et la préservation de l’identité. Dans le domaine de la santé, des unités médicales mobiles ont été déployées dans 31 localités du gouvernorat d’Al-Qods pour assurer des examens médicaux, des consultations et la distribution de médicaments, ainsi que l’orientation de 100 cas vers des structures spécialisées, portant à plus de 2.500 le nombre de bénéficiaires jusqu’en juin dernier, selon le rapport. En matière d’autonomisation économique, le rapport a relevé que l’Agence a soutenu la participation de six Start-ups palestiniennes au Salon « GITEX Africa » à Marrakech, dans le cadre de son programme d’incubation des jeunes entreprises. Ce dispositif a accompagné, au total, 34 entreprises, dont huit ont bénéficié de programmes d’accélération, tandis que trois ont lancé leurs activités commerciales en Italie et aux Émirats arabes unis. L’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif a, par ailleurs, organisé quatre sessions de formation dans l’import-export au profit d’environ 100 commerçants maqdessis, ainsi qu’un programme de formation aux métiers de l’artisanat ayant réuni 38 stagiaires et trois artisans marocains. Dans le domaine de l’enfance et de la jeunesse, le rapport met l'accent sur l’organisation de la 17e colonie de vacances annuelle « Manarat As-Salam » (Phare de la Paix), qui a bénéficié à 50 garçons et filles originaires d’Al-Qods, âgés de 11 à 14 ans. Le rapport jette la lumière également sur la tenue du « Hackathon Al-Qods 2026 », qui a réuni plus de 120 jeunes issus de huit universités palestiniennes, répartis en 35 équipes. Une enveloppe globale de 21.000 dollars a été consacrée aux équipes lauréates afin d’encourager le développement de solutions technologiques innovantes. Dans le secteur agricole, le rapport met en avant les interventions de l’Agence en faveur des agriculteurs d’Al-Qods, notamment le projet « Soumoud », lancé en janvier 2026 au profit de 250 agriculteurs, ainsi que le projet des « écoles aux champs », lancé en novembre 2025 afin de renforcer leurs capacités grâce à un apprentissage pratique et de terrain dans les différents domaines agricoles. Le bilan comprend aussi plusieurs initiatives culturelles et académiques, dont la participation au Salon international de l’édition et du livre de Rabat et l’organisation de rencontres visant à garantir une présence plus efficace de la narration palestinienne, ainsi que le partenariat avec des institutions marocaines et palestiniennes dans les domaines de l’éducation, de la formation, de la culture et de l’action sociale. Par ailleurs, le rapport s'attarde sur les répercussions de la guerre à Gaza et de la crise économique sur l’économie palestinienne, particulièrement sur les secteurs vitaux à Al-Qods, notamment l’emploi, le commerce et le tourisme, avec un focus sur les restrictions imposées à la circulation vers et depuis la ville sainte. Sur le plan de l’accompagnement social et sanitaire, l’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif a élargi son programme de parrainage des orphelins d’Al-Qods pour couvrir 350 orphelins de la bande de Gaza, en partenariat avec des associations locales. Le rapport fait également état d’un projet visant, dans une première phase, à fournir des prothèses au profit de 300 enfants amputés à Gaza à la suite de la guerre, et ce en coordination avec le ministère palestinien du Développement social et grâce à une contribution financière du Royaume du Maroc. En marge de la 52è session du Conseil des ministres des Affaires étrangères de l’OCI, l’Agence Bayt Mal Al-Qods Acharif organise une exposition de tableaux, de photographies et de publications afin de faire connaître ses programmes et ses projets à Al-Qods. The post Bayt Mal Al-Qods présente son bilan devant l’OCI appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Despite inflation trend down, stocks sustain losses amid selling pressure
items.description: The Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX dropped further Week-on-Week, WoW, amid selling pressure across sectors despite the fourth consecutive month of decline in headline inflation rate for the month of September 2026. Read Also: Nigeria’s Oil Assets: Oye demands probe into NNPC’s ₦11.2trn receivables Specifically, the NGX market capitalisation, which represents the total value of equities listed on the Exchange, dropped to N260.725 trillion last Friday from N161.260 trillion the previous week, as investors lost over N535 billion. Similarly, another market gauge, NGX All Share Index, ASI nosedived by 0.3% to close last Friday at 247539.73 points from 248,363.55 points the previous week. Analysis of trading showed that the market closed lower for the third consecutive week, as losses in Zenith Bank by -6 .5%, MTN Nigeria -1.8%, First HoldCo -3.9% and GTCO -4.4% contributed significantly to drag the ASI down WoW, bringing the Month-to-Date, MtD and Year-to-Date, YtD returns to -1.5% and +59.1%, respectively. On market activity, trading volume and value declined by 39.0% WoW and 38.0% WoW, respectively. On sector performance, the Banking declined by -3.1% and Insurance Index -0.1% , while the Oil & Gas Index rose by 3.1% and Consumer Goods 0.1% respectively. The Industrial Goods index closed flat. Commenting on the market outlook, analysts at Cordros Capital Limited, stated: “Looking ahead, we expect market sentiment to improve, supported by bargain hunting following recent price declines. Secondly, anticipation of third quarter, Q3 earnings releases and positioning ahead of upcoming dividend qualification dates, which could drive selective buying interest.” On their part, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, said: “The oil market’s movements may also influence expectations regarding inflation, energy costs and broader economic activity. Changes in crude prices can affect transportation, production and distribution costs, with potential implications for businesses across several sectors. However, the implications for individual companies will vary according to their exposure to energy prices, operating structures and ability to pass higher costs on to customers. Investors should therefore assess the potential impact of oil-price movements within the context of individual company fundamentals and the wider economic environment.” Vanguard News The post Despite inflation trend down, stocks sustain losses amid selling pressure appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria’s Oil Assets: Oye demands probe into NNPC’s ₦11.2trn receivables
items.description: The Chairman of the Alliance for Economic Research and Ethics, AERE, Dele Oye, has called for an independent probe into the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s ₦11.201 trillion receivables from the federation, demanding a transparent breakdown of the claims and the actual cost of securing the nation’s oil and gas assets. Read Also: NLC, Falana, activists rally Nigerians against petrol price hike, hardship Oye, who made the call in a policy analysis titled, “The ₦11.2 Trillion Bodyguard: A Receivable in a Security Uniform,” said the figures disclosed in NNPC’s 2025 annual report raised critical questions about the composition of the outstanding balance, the documentation of the underlying transactions and the reconciliation of obligations between the national oil company and the Federation. He, however, cautioned against interpreting the ₦11.2 trillion balance as money spent on security in 2025, stressing that the figure represents year-end receivables rather than expenditure incurred during the financial year. According to the report, NNPC’s other receivables from the Federation stood at ₦11.201 trillion at the end of December 2025, up from ₦8.840 trillion in 2024. The company broadly attributed the balance to advances to the Federation and costs incurred in protecting oil and gas assets under a government-approved framework. But Oye said the published accounts did not provide sufficient details to establish how much of the balance related to physical security, advances to government or other financial obligations. He said the government and NNPC must open the books to public scrutiny, insisting that the management of petroleum revenues and obligations should not be obscured by broad accounting descriptions. “The ₦11.2 trillion bodyguard is not a 2025 security bill,” Oye declared. ₦8.67trn energy-security balance reconciliation Explaining the accounting treatment, Oye said NNPC’s Note 24.2 recorded no energy-security expense for 2025, while an opening energy-security receivable of ₦8.672 trillion, carried forward from 2024, was reconciled in September 2025. The amount was offset against royalties, taxes and dividends due to the Federation as of December 2024, contributing to a reduction in total Federation receivables from ₦17.512 trillion to ₦11.201 trillion. He said the reconciliation did not remove the need for greater transparency, arguing that a receivable involving public funds, petroleum operations and government obligations required more detailed disclosure. “That does not end the transparency question; it finally starts it properly. A receivable from the Federation is not an invoice from a private customer. It sits at the intersection of public finance, petroleum operations and sovereign authority. When the label is broad, scrutiny must become narrow,” he said. Oye also explained that the energy-security framework was not limited to the protection of pipelines and other petroleum infrastructure. Under the Petroleum Industry Act framework cited by NNPC, the label also covered its supplier-of-last-resort role and, during the regulated petrol period, price-under-recovery obligations. He described under-recovery as the difference between the actual landing cost of imported petrol and the regulated selling price, noting that exchange-rate movements could widen the gap. However, he said NNPC’s 2025 report did not separately quantify the foreign-exchange component. In his view, the broad classification combined physical asset protection with oil-market and public-finance arrangements that should be accounted for separately. Demands public register of costs To address the disclosure gaps, Oye called for a publicly accessible register separating physical oil and gas asset security costs, supplier-of-last-resort and price-under-recovery obligations, and advances to the Federation. He proposed a three-column reconciliation showing, for each category, the legal authority, beneficiaries, supporting invoices, cash status, amounts offset against government obligations and measurable outcomes. “Nigeria should therefore insist on a three-column public reconciliation: physical asset security; supplier-of-last-resort/price-under-recovery support; and advances to the Federation. Each column should show the legal authority, beneficiary, invoice, cash status, offset status and measurable result,” he said. The AERE chairman said the disclosures should be supported by verifiable evidence of the protection and maintenance of the infrastructure concerned, enabling Nigerians to distinguish actual security expenditure from other financial arrangements recorded in the company’s books. He argued that a credible accountability framework must document the costs incurred, transactions completed, obligations settled and results achieved. Questions over NNPC’s profit growth Beyond the receivables, Oye raised questions about the composition of NNPC’s reported profit after tax of ₦7.183 trillion in 2025, compared with ₦5.414 trillion in 2024. He acknowledged the company’s reported achievements, including peak crude and condensate production of 1.77 million barrels per day, its highest level in five years, and a declared dividend of ₦5.8 trillion. However, he noted that revenue fell 24 per cent to ₦34.517 trillion, while gross profit declined by about 20 per cent to ₦9.374 trillion, even as profit after tax increased. According to him, the accounts showed that other income rose from ₦3.392 trillion in 2024 to ₦8.416 trillion in 2025, while an impairment charge of ₦753.557 billion in 2024 became a reversal of ₦325.432 billion in 2025. Oye said NNPC attributed its largest other-income category, described as “sundry income”, to items including Trans-Forcados pipeline income, crude-processing fees, miscellaneous income from joint-venture operators and a write-back connected to an Amenam-Kpono stock-overlift claim. He stressed that the figures did not invalidate the reported profit but warranted further explanation of the factors driving the increase. “None of that makes the profit unreal. But it does make the simple victory dance incomplete. When a company’s profit grows while core revenue and gross profit retreat, citizens deserve to know which cash-generating operations did the lifting, which accounting estimates moved, and which one-off items may not return for an encore,” he said. Oye added: “The numbers deserve applause before they receive interrogation.” He said Nigerians should be able to see, line by line, how value was generated, what was owed, how obligations were settled and what benefits were delivered. Pipeline maintenance disclosure The AERE chairman also questioned the presentation of pipeline maintenance costs in NNPC’s accounts, warning against drawing conclusions from a single expense category without examining the broader cost structure. He noted that the line item for pipeline maintenance costs fell from ₦149.478 billion in 2024 to ₦13.813 billion in 2025, a decline of 90.76 per cent. However, he said “other direct costs” rose from ₦566.540 billion to ₦1.277 trillion over the same period. According to NNPC’s disclosures cited in the analysis, the broader category includes the maintenance and operation of wells, production facilities, pipelines and processing infrastructure, as well as integrity management, repairs and field support. Oye said the figures did not establish that physical pipeline maintenance had fallen by 90 per cent, but exposed a reporting gap that made it difficult for the public to determine whether work had been postponed, reclassified, captured under another cost centre or performed more efficiently. “So the accounts do not prove that physical maintenance collapsed by 90%. They prove that the public cannot tell, from the published categories, whether work was postponed, reclassified, embedded in another cost centre or carried out more efficiently. That distinction is not a footnote; it is the governance issue,” he said. He called on NNPC to publish an asset-integrity scorecard for each major trunk line, detailing planned and actual maintenance, incidents, downtime, integrity spending and independent inspection results. “A pipeline is not a metaphor. It either holds pressure or it holds a press conference,” he added. Calls for accountability, not publicity Oye said NNPC’s reported financial and production achievements should be acknowledged but accompanied by stronger disclosure of the financial arrangements, future obligations and operational results behind the figures. He also called for greater transparency over forward-sale commitments, arguing that a public commitments calendar was necessary to clarify obligations associated with future deliveries and their implications for domestic supply. He cautioned that memoranda of understanding and public announcements could not substitute for verifiable operational performance, particularly where refinery operations were concerned. “NNPC’s 2025 accounts contain real achievements: stronger reported profit, improved production and a notable dividend declaration. They also show a financial architecture in which major public questions can still hide inside broad labels, offsets and future-delivery obligations,” he said. “The ₦11.2 trillion figure is not proof that ₦11.2 trillion was spent on security in 2025. It is a very large Federation receivable whose composition deserves a public ledger.” He added that the maintenance figures did not prove that pipeline upkeep had disappeared, but highlighted a disclosure structure inadequate for a strategic national asset. Oye urged the government and NNPC to strengthen the documentation and reconciliation of petroleum revenues, expenditure and obligations, insisting that public accountability must extend beyond headline profits and production figures. “Nigeria does not need another acronym, another relaunch or another headline with a ribbon around it. It needs a receipt: names, dates, invoices, barrels, offsets, performance and cash,” he said.
